articles.body:

articles.title: Florian Wirtz helping to unlock Alexander Isak at Liverpool as Antonio Silva shines for Bournemouth - The Radar
articles.summary: Alexander Isak added two more goals to his tally against Club Brugge and earned praise for his all-round play, so what's behind the Liverpool striker's return to form? Plus, the Bournemouth summer signing already providing value for money under Marco Rose
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺Secrets behind Isak's return to form 🔺Bournemouth's next defensive gem 🔺A player to watch this weekend

Isak's Wirtz connection and left-foot finishing

Alexander Isak reached double figures for the season with his two goals in Liverpool's 3-0 victory over Club Brugge . His finishes, a first-time effort from a cut-back and a dink over the goalkeeper in a one-on-one, showed he is playing with confidence again.

The 27-year-old is swiftly putting an injury-hit first season at Liverpool behind him. He faces Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday having become only the eighth player in the club's history to score in six consecutive away games in all competitions.

Andoni Iraola praised the quality of his link-up play after the game against Club Brugge. His total of 44 touches was his highest in any fixture this season and came three days after he recorded his next-highest total with 39 in the 4-0 win over Manchester United .

The numbers are encouraging for Iraola as he tries to bring cohesion to his attack. He wants Isak to be involved in Liverpool's approach play. But the striker is benefitting from spending more time where is most dangerous too: in the opposition penalty area.

His box touches per 90 minutes have leapt by 60 per cent in the Premier League this season. He is also averaging 53 per cent more shots. But the increase has been most dramatic in his numbers for goals and expected goals, both of which have doubled.

Isak is scoring more because he is getting better-quality chances. And Florian Wirtz, another expensive signing who struggled last term, has played a vital role in improving the striker's service.

Wednesday's game provided more evidence of the understanding developing between the two players. According to Opta, Wirtz found Isak with 10 passes, nearly twice as many as anyone else.

Wirtz also made more passes to Isak than any team-mate on Sunday against Manchester United, with six, including one from which Isak nearly scored in the 75th minute. In the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace, there was a cute pass to set up his goal.

Going further back, it was Wirtz who played Isak in behind for the cut-back which led to Liverpool's penalty against Brentford. Against Brighton and Nottingham Forest, there were passes over the top which would have put Isak through if not for loose touches.

In total in the Premier League, Wirtz has made 29 passes to Isak - 10 more than anyone else. He is finding Isak at a rate of 3.35 times per 90 minutes, up from 2.57 times per 90 minutes last season.

Data from Gradient Sports highlights that he is providing quality as well as quantity with his passes. Wirtz ranks behind only Arsenal midfielder Martin Odegaard in the Premier League this season for passes into a dangerous position, with 62.

Of course, the relationship between a striker and his No 10 has to work both ways. And Isak, fitter and sharper than at any point in his Liverpool career following an uninterrupted pre-season, is certainly doing his bit when it comes to his movement.

According to Opta, he ranks top among all Premier League players this season for runs in behind, runs ending in the opposition box and runs making him an option for a cross. He is also top for runs followed by team shots and team goals.

The volume and quality of Isak's runs is making Wirtz's task easier when it comes to providing service. But importantly, Isak has also added variety and unpredictability to his finishing.

This season in the Premier League, he has scored four goals with his weaker left foot compared to three with his right. Eleven games in, it is already his highest total of left-footed goals in a season since arriving in the Premier League with Newcastle in 2022.

Gradient's data shows a sharp rise in his left-footed shooting. Isak has taken 37.9 per cent of his shots on his left this term, compared to roughly 15 per cent across the previous two seasons.

As with Wirtz's passes, it is a matter of quality as well as quantity.

Gradient's grading system, in which players are graded out of 100 in a wide range of categories based on the quality of their execution, shows Isak's left-footed shooting grade has improved across the last three seasons, from 60, to 70 to 75, meaning he has gone from the 46th percentile to the 94th in the space of two years.

The improvement has made him more difficult to defend against.

Consider his second goal against Ipswich in September, when both Dara O'Shea and Kjell Scherpen were anticipating a right-footed shot, only for Isak to shift the ball onto his left and score.

Brentford were similarly flummoxed by his goal at the Gtech Community Stadium in October, when he fired a left-footed finish through a crowd of bodies a split second after controlling Bradley Barcola's back-post knockdown using his right.

With Wirtz picking out his runs, with the goals flowing, and with growing trust in his weaker foot, Isak will feel confident of extending his scoring run in Sunday's Merseyside derby.

Bournemouth face Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports+ on Sunday, having won a club-record 10 straight games while only conceding three goals. If there is one area which encapsulates this club's capacity to renew and rebuild, it is their defence.

Over the course of the last two summers, Bournemouth have lost five starting defenders in Dean Huijsen, Illia Zabarnyi, Milos Kerkez, Alex Jimenez and Marcos Senesi. An entire backline dismantled. And yet they have become defensively stronger this season.

Bournemouth rank among the Premier League's top four sides for expected goals against and shots allowed this season. Only Arsenal have allowed fewer shots on target.

Bournemouth's goals conceded column is skewed by their 5-1 loss to Chelsea in early October. But they haven't lost since. Their 10-game winning run has included seven clean sheets.

Alongside James Hill, Antonio Silva has played a big part. He already looks like one of the signings of the season following his £25.7m arrival from Benfica. Carry on as he has started and the club will be confident of one day banking another hefty profit.

For now, though, they can just enjoy the contribution of the latest centre-back to demonstrate elite quality for the club. Silva was no unknown. He joined as a Portugal international with 183 senior appearances for his boyhood club Benfica behind him.

But it still took shrewd judgement to know his qualities would transfer to the Premier League. And Bournemouth have demonstrated a handy knack for getting these things right.

In an interview with Sky Sports in August , Joao Nuno Fonseca, a former coach in the Benfica development team, highlighted the quality of Silva's anticipation and his ability to read the game, all of which has been evident since his arrival at Bournemouth.

Gradient Sports, whose analysts grade player actions by execution quality, give him a positioning grade of 86.7 out of 100 this term, putting him among the Premier League's best defenders. Only Jeremy Jacquet beats his 79.5 one-vs-one defending grade.

Silva has also shown his technical quality. Crucially for Marco Rose, who favours quick, vertical passes like Iraola, the 23-year-old is a forward-thinking passer. Only Jan Paul van Hecke has completed more line-breaking passes among centre-backs this season.

He is comfortable punching passes through midfield and is also able to switch the play with long diagonals. According to Gradient, he scores above his positional average in a wide-range of passing categories, demonstrating the extent of his offering on the ball.

After Huijsen and Zabarnyi, now at Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, Silva looks like the latest Bournemouth centre-back destined to reach the very top.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

Quentin Timber , brother of Arsenal's Jurrien, is earning positive reviews at Crystal Palace. They've won five of the 12 games he has started this season and only one of the six he hasn't. It's Hull next for the Eagles, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

Seven Premier League games are live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting when Nottingham Forest host Chelsea at 8pm on Friday.

Saturday sees Ipswich Town take on Aston Villa at 5.30pm.

There are five games live on Sunday, with Brighton hosting Newcastle , Crystal Palace facing Hull , Fulham taking on Bournemouth and Sunderland hosting Tottenham all at 2.05pm before Arsenal face Manchester City at 4.30pm.

Last week's column examined the qualities that make David Raya the Premier League's best goalkeeper and also featured a look at Newcastle's pressing problem under Matthias Jaissle .

articles.title: Sunderland 1-1 Jagiellonia Bialystok: Black Cats maintain Europa League play-off push with draw
articles.summary: Report as Sunderland are held 1-1 by Jagiellonia Bialystok in the Europa League; Black Cats expressed disappointment after some Jagiellonia fans were in attendance in home area at the Stadium of Light; hosts struck early in second half through Timur Tutierov; Kamil Jozwiak soon levelled
articles.body:
A UEFA away supporter ban had been imposed on Jagiellonia for Thursday's fixture on Wearside.

However, in the opening minutes of the match, police and stewards were seen attending to some disruption in a home area in the ground.

A club statement said: "Sunderland AFC is disappointed that a number of Jagiellonia Bialystok supporters were present in home areas of the Stadium of Light during tonight's UEFA Europa League fixture.

"Jagiellonia Bialystok were subject to a UEFA away supporter ban for tonight's Matchday 5 fixture, following a disciplinary sanction imposed by European football's governing body.

"In the build-up to the match, the club had put measures in place in line with this sanction and maintained regular communication with our supporters, Jagiellonia Bialystok and UEFA. Unfortunately, Jagiellonia Bialystok failed to engage and cooperate on this matter.

"We are disappointed that these measures and communications were disregarded by some visiting supporters and will review the circumstances surrounding their entry to the stadium."

Jagiellonia Bialystok are yet to respond.

As for game itself, Sunderland were left frustrated again in their Europa League campaign after another draw.

The Black Cats enjoyed the best of the first-half chances through Malick Fofana and Nilson Angulo, but the visitors had an opportunity when Robin Roefs saved Kajetan Szmyt's free-kick.

Sunderland struck early in the second half through Timur Tutierov's header, his second goal in the competition, but Kamil Jozwiak levelled only minutes later after capitalising on a mistake at the back.

A point means the Wearsiders stay in the knockout phase play-off places after being held to their second draw from five games in the competition.

30: CHANCE! Le Fee latches on to Vital's underhit back pass and then lays the ball across the area for the unmarked Angulo - only for Kobayashi to get back and make a brilliant goal-saving block.

42: SAVE! Roefs does well at full stretch to get two hands to beat clear Szmyt's well-struck effort.

45+1: CLOSE! So nearly a wonder goal from Hume, but the skipper's thumping volley flashes inches past the far post.

47: GOAL! Tuterov, unmarked at the back post, taps in Le Fee's inviting ball across the six-yard box to lift the Stadium of Light.

52: GOAL! The visitors are level after a terrible mistake at the back by Reinildo, whose underhit back pass is intercepted by Jozwiak, who rounds Roefs, before scoring into the empty net.

61: SAVE! Roefs comes to Sunderland's rescue with an excellent low stop to turn behind Szmyt's drive after the home side again give the ball away in a bad area.

79: CHANCE Imaz's effort is straight at a grateful Roefs when the sub seemed certain to score from 10 yards out after being picked out by a pull back from the left byline.

82: BLOCK! Sunderland corner from the right and a huge block by Romanchuk as Angulo cut back inside and fired goalwards and that looked to be heading for the corner.

90+1: SAVE! Roefs comes to Sunderland's rescue after another mistake at the back, this time from Meunier, who allows Agbonifo to beat him to a long ball up field and break clear one on one with the 'keeper.

articles.title: Brighton 4-0 CS Universitatea Craiova: Ibrahim Osman stars as Seagulls bounce back with Conference League win
articles.summary: Match report as Brighton beat 10-man Universitatea Craiova 4-0 in the Conference League; Ibrahim Osman scored his first Brighton goals in the win; Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign; Osman also set up Charalampos Kostoulas for a third
articles.body:
Talk of the high-flying Seagulls potentially being shock Premier League title contenders this season was dampened slightly by Sunday's surprise 2-0 defeat at Hull.

Winger Osman finished a flowing move to set Albion on course to avoid a further unexpected defeat before Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign to double the lead.

Romanian champions Craiova were left with little hope of a comeback at the Amex Stadium when defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off in the 39th minute for stamping on the ankle of Matt O'Riley.

Osman set up Charalampos Kostoulas for the third goal before quickly claiming his second with a fine individual effort as Brighton made it 10 points from four games in the competition on a bitterly cold evening in Sussex.

3: GOAL! The move started with Kadioglu down the right and he then picks out Kostoulas in the box, who in turn feeds Hinshelwood in space and his low driven ball to the back post is tapped home by the unmarked Osman.

33: GOAL! Brighton double their lead as the visitors play a risky crossfield pass that is intercepted by De Cuyper, who then beats Popescu with a delightful right-footed curler from distance that leaves the 'keeper rooted to his line as the ball goes in off the post.

39: RED! The referee did not need long to look at that, with Screciu shown a straight red for that dangerous-looking tackle on O'Riley.

46: SAVE! Azeez, with his first touch since coming on, whips a lovely ball in from the right and Hinshelwood must have thought he had scored with a bullet header - but Popescu responds with a brilliant save.

61: GOAL! Osman feeds Kostoulas in the area and from a tight angle, the Greek's low drive beats Popescu at his near post.

78: CLOSE! Azeez twists and turns on the right edge of the box, but his curler is inches away from finding the top corner with the 'keeper motionless.

Hurzeler reserves praise for Osman after brace for Brighton

"He [Osman] showed a really good performance today," said Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler.

"We know that his biggest quality is one against one, especially against teams who are sitting in a low block.

"This is very helpful to have these one-against-one players. He showed a very impressive style today."

Asked about the decision not to loan out Osman again, Hurzeler said: "It's not the Conference League (campaign) that was the key.

"The key was his performance and his effort and his development he showed through the loans. But also his effort and work ethic and his quality he showed in pre-season.

"That was the key for us to make this decision. Therefore he is a big part of our team. We need a good depth in the squad and we are very happy that he is here now."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Loren Juarros: "No me arrepiento de lo que he hecho"
articles.standfirst: El ya ex director deportivo se despidió en La Rosaleda
articles.summary: El ya ex director deportivo se despidió en La Rosaleda
articles.body: Loren Juarros puso punto final a su etapa en el Málaga CF con un discurso de despedida en el que defendió el proyecto desarrollado durante sus tres años y medio en Martiricos. El ya exdirector deportivo se marchó con sentimientos encontrados, entre la tristeza por abandonar un club al que considera que todavía le queda mucho potencial y la satisfacción por el trabajo realizado. "Me voy satisfecho por dejar al Málaga CF en Primera División", aseguró. El burgalés reivindicó especialmente su apuesta por la cantera como eje del crecimiento de la entidad. Una filosofía que considera que ha dado resultados y que debe mantenerse en el futuro. "Mi mayor acierto ha sido venir con la idea que tengo y haber sido capaz de apostar por este modelo de cantera", explicó. En esa línea, recordó el impulso dado a La Academia, la puesta en marcha de la Ciudad Deportiva y la presencia de 14 futbolistas de las categorías inferiores en la primera plantilla. Juarros también reconoció que se marcha sin haber alcanzado todos los objetivos que tenía en mente. Le hubiera gustado conseguir la estabilidad del equipo en Primera División, aunque considera que el club ha avanzado de manera importante desde su llegada. "Me voy con la pena de dejar un proyecto que está acabado e inacabado. Me hubiera gustado estabilizarlo en Primera", reconoció. Sobre los motivos de su destitución, no esquivó la situación clasificatoria del equipo, que acumula 13 jornadas sin ganar. Loren admitió que los resultados tienen un peso determinante, aunque defendió que el rendimiento del Málaga no siempre ha reflejado lo merecido sobre el terreno de juego. "El equipo, en muchos partidos, ha merecido algo más de lo que ha obtenido. Creo que la suerte no nos ha acompañado demasiado", señaló. También aseguró que siempre trabajó dentro de los límites económicos establecidos por el club. Uno de los momentos más significativos de su comparecencia llegó al valorar sus posibles errores. "Quizá no haber sido tan ambicioso en algunas cosas o no haber tensionado en determinados aspectos", reconoció. El burgalés explicó que prefirió mantenerse fiel a sus principios y priorizar la inversión en la cantera frente a operaciones de mayor coste para el primer equipo. "Podría haber volcado más recursos en el primer equipo y haber dejado de lado a la cantera, sí. Pero no me arrepiento de lo que he hecho", sentenció. Por último, mostró su confianza en la plantilla para revertir la delicada situación deportiva y pidió que se mantenga el modelo de cantera con la llegada de la nueva dirección deportiva. Considera que quienes asuman el mando encontrarán un club más fuerte que el que recibió en 2023. "Estos jugadores van a seguir creciendo, compitiendo dentro de sus posibilidades y ganando partidos", afirmó en un último mensaje de respaldo al vestuario.

articles.title: Jens Berthel Askou interview: Former Motherwell coach transforming Toulouse with commitment to possession football
articles.summary: In this exclusive interview with Sky Sports, Toulouse head coach Jens Berthel Askou explains why he remains so committed to the possession football that he played at Motherwell and how he is now using those same principles to help transform his new team in Ligue 1...
articles.body:
But Askou has become a very different coach to the one who had been at Horsens in his native Denmark. "My regret from back then is that I did not implement what I really preferred to do. I just needed a little bit of time as a coach to be brave enough to do it."

The 44-year-old former Norwich City defender is proving himself brave enough now. In fact, he has become one of the most tactically interesting coaches in European football, having transformed Motherwell and now beginning to do the same at Toulouse.

Just, who is now at Swansea, did indeed link up with Askou at Motherwell and helped the team to play some of the most stylish stuff in Scotland. Their possession statistics leapt from 39 per cent to 59 per cent, playing a brand of football few thought possible.

"Motherwell just gave me the next level of confidence and belief," says Askou. If it could work in Scotland, where his side finished fourth having briefly been in a title race, then it could work anywhere. "It is a very similar journey," he says of his new role at Toulouse.

Again, he has taken over a team unaccustomed to having the ball. Toulouse ranked second bottom for possession in Ligue 1 last season. Now, they are up among the top seven. "If we compare our style now to last season, it is quite a big change," he says.

"From day one against Lyon, we dominated and created chances. The plan is to press the opponent as high as possible for as long as possible and to keep them under siege and attack relentlessly without the ball. It is not just a game plan. It is an identity."

Life in southern France is a little different to his previous assignment. "People are still eating outside here," he says, smiling broadly. "It is fantastic, a wonderful city. But I loved the west end of Glasgow too. It was a very cool place to live. I miss the people."

On the pitch, the parallels are obvious. As at Motherwell, he has been met with some resistance and the results are lagging a little behind the data with Toulouse in midtable. "The underlying numbers put us in fourth. It is easy to see what we are doing."

Askou once said that his ideas require months to take shape. "I have to correct myself a bit," he says now. "It is actually possible to teach the basics in two weeks and be competitive in six. You can see a difference in how much the players want the ball."

Even so, he is still questioned when these players make errors that lead to goals. The accusations of overplaying are familiar now. "It is one of those stupid paradoxes that still exist in football." Coaches who concede due to underplaying are rarely called out.

"When teams go long and concede goals because they are having to defend more, that is not being criticised as a style-of-play goal," Askou explains. "Even though, when they play those longer balls, they are completely spread all over the park when they lose it."

His commitment to his football is total and it has been a process not an epiphany to reach this point. But he cites his time as assistant manager at Copenhagen as being key. "That opened my eyes. I realised that my next chance to be head coach, I had to go all in."

He explains: "I just felt from a personal point of view that if I am lucky enough to do this for the next 20 years and I am going to invest so much of my energy, my time and my life into this, when it takes a huge toll on my family, then it has be fun, it has to be exciting."

Players respond to it. He urges them to "remember why we fell in love with this game when we were kids" and that means wanting the ball. With time, Askou believes that he has matured enough as a leader to know that sticking to his principles is everything.

"Now, I have enough experience and knowledge as a leader to be calm and patient and spread that bravery, to really make that bravery grow roots in the squad and in the club. That way it is strong enough to withstand all the resistance that can come."

It is curious to note that his predecessor at Toulouse, Carles Martinez, has gone on to become Bayer Leverkusen head coach after doing some fine work in France. "His intention was to adapt to a more Spanish, possession-based style," notes Askou.

But Martinez took a pragmatic approach last term. "After the first season, they changed a little bit. They went back to a more direct counter-attacking style." Do not expect his successor ever to revert to those tactics. "There is no turning back now," he insists.

He is trying to stay open-minded, of course. "I have to keep reminding myself that the reason I am here now is because I have allowed myself to be open to new ideas." Football evolves and coaches are obliged to make tactical adjustments to prosper.

"I cannot keep copying what I am doing for the next 10 years because then someone is going to blast right past me. You have to be curious, you have to be innovative." But there are non-negotiables. His players will keep taking the ball under pressure.

"To give yourself the best opportunity to perform, the consistency of approach and the principles have to be there," Askou continues. "The overall approach to the game in terms of being brave and trying to dominate is never going to change."

How far can that take Toulouse? He points to the success of Bodo/Glimt in Norway and Como in Italy as evidence that teams can disrupt the natural order. "There are possibilities everywhere in football." He sees Brighton in England as another example.

"Through strategic decisions and bravery in recruitment, by allowing a progressive coach to develop a style, you now find them towards the top of the strongest league in the world. The focus on data is allowing for clubs to have more innovative approaches.

"I just feel blessed to have found another opportunity with people who are supportive, enthusiastic and humble. If we keep overperforming then eventually some of the light will end up on the players and also on me and the other good people here at this club."

His football has put him in that spotlight. The aim now? "To raise the bar. To be even more ambitious and brave." You had better believe him. And if Jens Berthel Askou ever wants to link up with a former player again, you can be certain they will believe him now too.

articles.title: Senne Lammens in spotlight - will Man Utd drop their goalkeeper?
articles.summary: Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens made two major mistakes in the 2-2 draw with Sporting - could Mauricio Pochettino drop his goalkeeper?
articles.body:
After a first season at Manchester United that drew little but praise, goalkeeper Senne Lammens is under the microscope like never before.

A bad mistake that gifted Sporting their second goal on Wednesday, having earlier conceded a clumsy penalty, followed several other errors so far this season.

The 24-year-old Belgium international also made an error at the World Cup in the summer, spilling a shot that led to Spain's winning goal in the 88th minute of their quarter-final.

"I don't know [at what point Manchester United drop him]," legendary Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel told CBS Sports on Wednesday.

"Mauricio Pochettino has come in and brought his own staff. That means he's got a new goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him.

"[At the World Cup] he came on against Spain and made a bit of a mistake. Mikel Merino scored and they got knocked out. I feel he's lost a little bit of confidence from that mistake and hasn't really recovered.

"As a goalkeeper, when you're not on your best form, you need your defenders in front of you to help you out. The sad truth is that they haven't been able to do that and that makes it so much worse. I like him a lot but today was not a great day for him."

Director of football Jason Wilcox and United's data team overruled Ruben Amorim when they opted to sign Lammens from Royal Antwerp for £18.1m in September 2025.

Amorim wanted Argentina World Cup winner Emiliano Martinez, who was left waiting for a deadline day call that never came to seal a move from Aston Villa.

United felt Lammens had the attributes to become one of the world's best goalkeepers. At 24, he is still young. Schmeichel was 27 when he joined United in 1991. Edwin van der Sar was 34 when he left Fulham in 2005. Both had hundreds of senior appearances behind them. Lammens has just over 100, more than half of them with Royal Antwerp.

Although he made the odd error last season, Lammens did nothing to suggest Wilcox and co had got it wrong.

After releasing Turkey international Altay Bayindir, who replaced Andre Onana as first choice at the start of last season and is back on loan in Turkey with Trabzonspor, they signed 36-year-old Wales international Karl Darlow as back-up this term.

Darlow finished last season as first choice at Leeds. But he only started 30 league games in three seasons with the Elland Road outfit. Also on the bench in Lisbon was Tom Heaton. The 40-year-old has not played in a senior game since February 2023.

Mistakes earlier in the season – former United midfielder Paul Scholes claimed in September '"the jury is still out" on whether Lammens is truly top class – have brought increased analysis. His positioning for Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal for Liverpool on Sunday was questioned externally, even if United focused their attentions on Bradley Barcola shoving into the wall.

Just 75 seconds after getting down to make an excellent save from Luis Suarez's first penalty, Lammens recklessly charged out and upended Maxi Araujo, even though Noussair Mazraoui seemed to be in a position to deal with it.

Then, after two Bruno Fernandes goals at the start of the second period had turned the Champions League tie in the visitors' favour, Lammens reached to collect a high ball and inexplicably dropped it in front of Suarez, who applied the overhead kick finish.

Understandably, there was sympathy in the dressing room.

"This team is a family," said striker Joshua Zirkzee. "There's no-one who will suffer by themselves.

"Senne is a great goalkeeper and mistakes happen. In this moment, we just give him space. I'm not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne's a great kid. He's got a good head on him. We didn't draw because of him, and we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game."

Jimenez the key to Lammens bouncing back

Toni Jimenez is Pochettino's long-time goalkeeping coach.

His arrival triggered the exit of Craig Mawson, who had been with Manchester United since 2019. Connor King is Jimenez's assistant but a relative newcomer himself, having joined from Burnley in 2026.

By its nature, goalkeeping at the highest level can be a mental challenge as well as a technical one. As Onana discovered, flaws can quickly become major issues and once the spotlight is shining, the attention is fierce.

Lammens has given the impression privately of being strong. He has seemed remarkably unaffected by his World Cup torment – his mistake against Spain came after he was introduced as a 71st-minute replacement for injured veteran Thibaut Courtois with the quarter-final delicately poised at 1-1. But only he knows the full picture.

Jimenez will be Pochettino's guide over what to do about the situation, although for now, Lammens' head coach is behind him.

"This type of thing happens," he said. "That is football. Football is about making mistakes.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."

Following Wednesday's draw in Lisbon, Pochettino highlighted "two things" that need to improve if United are to start winning matches on a regular basis.

The first of those is the club's preferred goalkeeper. Of the 17 Premier League goalkeepers to have played a minimum of 10 matches in all competitions in this campaign, Lammens has the second-worst save success rate, keeping out just 60.2% of the shots he has faced. Only Coventry's Carl Rushworth (54.4%) has fared worse so far this season.

Lammens also ranks bottom of those 17 goalkeepers for clean sheet ratio (6.3%).

And there is substance to the suggestion that Lammens has declined in 2026-27. He made just one error leading to a goal in the entirety of last season in contrast to two already in this campaign. The data also shows that he is currently preventing far fewer goals.

The second "thing", however, has significant bearing on the first.

Clean sheets and conceding fewer goals are clearly a collective responsibility, particularly for the "defensive line" that Pochettino referenced on Wednesday - and United's defence has collectively struggled this season.

They have now let in 36 goals in all competitions, the most of any team in Europe's top five leagues. They have also conceded five penalties and received five red cards - both the second-highest tallies among Europe's elite divisions.

So is Lammens more error-prone this season? Apparently yes. But he's also playing behind a defence that, on current form, may not inspire too much confidence in their goalkeeper.

articles.title: Premier League predictions: Chris Sutton v Kings of Leon drummer Nathan Followill - & AI
articles.summary: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on Kings of Leon drummer Nathan Followill with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League games.
articles.body:
Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke should probably turn his phone off if the Gunners fall behind against Manchester City on Sunday.

Chris Sutton's predictions guest this week, Kings of Leon drummer and City fan Nathan Followill, is good friends with Kroenke - and says he will be in touch if the game is going City's way.

"I'm super excited for this weekend and I've got my smack talk ready for Josh already," Followill told BBC Sport.

"I've heard about the City fans with their inflatable bananas and I need to get myself one. My wife is going to be like 'er, an inflatable banana just arrived in the mail - do you know anything about that?'

"We are going to win 4-2 so I will be texting Josh throughout the game... and, after Erling Haaland's second goal, I will send him a picture of me kissing the banana!"

AI has also made its predictions, and you can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

Followill has supported City for more than 20 years , external and his children have followed in his footsteps by becoming Blues, despite the best efforts of his next-door neighbour in Nashville, as well as Kroenke.

"When my kids were born, they both received a full Arsenal kit - head to toe - in the mail from Josh," he explained.

"Both times, they were returned to sender - instantly.

"My son and daughter are both City fans now, but my neighbour, Jeremy Connor, is Tottenham , and I mean flying the flag full on.

"When they lose, you can hear him screaming - and when they win, you can hear him screaming too.

"His son is trying to convert my son to Spurs and I am like 'that is never going to happen in this house!'"

Chris Sutton and Nathan Followill were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

Chelsea have scored and conceded 20 goals so far this season, which kind of sums up where they are at.

Xabi Alonso's side have also lost as many league games - five - as Manchester United , and United are in crisis.

Alonso is not under pressure, or anything like that, but if they lose this game too, you can imagine the mood of the club - and it won't be good.

Apparently their fans were singing 'you don't know what you're doing' at him after their defeat by Leeds - which is what they sang at me when I was there.

Alonso needs to decide on a shape and a way of playing, and stick with it.

Anything could happen here, because Nottingham Forest 's form is hardly convincing either.

They tore Manchester City apart in their previous home game, before the international break, but can they really dig out another result like that here?

I think they will go about it in a similar way, and be aggressive and have a real go at Chelsea ... and I don't see Chelsea 's defence keeping them out.

Nathan's prediction: No-one thought Forest would beat us, and while Chelsea need a big result, I can see Forest getting a point here. 1-1

We talked about Leeds on the Monday Night Club and how they have upgraded their team with the players Daniel Farke bought over the summer.

Farke strengthened in the areas he needed to improve, but is still trusting some of the players who did well for him last season - the likes of Jayden Bogle and James Justin, who have been outstanding.

They are a really well-balanced team and they have good depth to their squad too. The only criticism would be that they are not usually free-scoring - they hit four against Chelsea but before then they had only managed 10 goals in their first 10 league games.

Leeds do not give much away at the back either, though, and I think that will be key in this game.

When I watch Coventry they are dynamic with their counter-attacks and I always fancy them to nick a goal like that.

Not this time, however. Leeds might take a while to break them down, but I think they will come out on top.

Nathan's prediction: Coventry play in sky blue too? Part of the reason I became a Manchester City fan was the kit, and I have always gravitated towards teams in light blue, so I am going to go with Coventry here. 0-1

I am at this game for 5 Live and I am not expecting much to change for Manchester United .

No-one thought it was going to be easy for Mauricio Pochettino to go in at United and turn things around. He has taken over a complete rabble.

United's draw in Lisbon on Wednesday was chaotic, but you also have to consider how Sporting have not got going in the Portuguese league or the Champions League this season.

That was not a great Sporting side. They are pretty average and Brentford will be a much bigger test.

The Bees are supremely well-organised and will be full of confidence, too, after putting four goals past Everton on Monday. They were against 10 men for the entire second half, but were 2-0 up by then anyway.

Pochettino needs something to cling to, but for him picking that backline must be like pinning the tail on the donkey. Whoever he picks, they are not very good.

I really want to be more positive about United, because I heard from quite a few of their fans last weekend, but this prediction is about as positive as I can be about them at the moment.

Nathan's prediction: It is tough for me to talk about United because in America we have a saying 'don't kick a man when he's down' and it's pretty rough for them right now... but I'm not going to lie, it is nice to see United this low in the table.

I don't think it is the manager that is the problem for United right now, so I don't think Pochettino coming in is going to be an instant fix. They've got some growing pains to get through, and I won't be disappointed to watch that.

When I watch the Premier League at home, Brentford always cracks me up because I am huge fan of The Office and I just imagine a bunch of David Brents out there, just running around the pitch, which is a very funny thing for me.

I know I just said don't kick a man when he's down, but I don't think United would be nice to us if we were down there... so, I think the David Brents are going to win. 1-2

I actually think Villa will win this game 2-1 but I want to make it clear the scoreline I have gone for is from my commentary colleague, Alistair Bruce-Ball, who is an Ipswich fan - a fake one, but still a fan.

I asked him about this game when we were in Belgium for Liverpool 's Champions League game on Wednesday. He will be at Portman Road on Saturday for 5 Live and he is backing the Tractor Boys to get something, so I am doing the same out of respect for him.

Ipswich really need a result too. They have gone five league games without a win and, with Hull and Coventry both winning last week, they are the lowest placed of the promoted sides.

That is never a good thing, and it feels like Gary O'Neil's side are in a precarious position at the moment, where they are getting sucked towards the bottom three.

I've been surprised to see Villa hit a bit of a sticky patch too, with three successive league draws and no wins in six in all competitions, so it will be interesting to see if they are any better here.

Nathan's prediction: Villa have had some surprising results recently but I do think they will win this. 1-3

I was in Bruges to watch Liverpool in midweek and it was interesting to see two of their players who came in for some heavy flak last season, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, both shine.

Isak is looking like the player who Liverpool thought they signed in 2025. He is finding his rhythm, and Wirtz also seems to be in a really good place confidence-wise. When I watch them now, it feels like something is going to happen.

There are other positives for Reds boss Andoni Iraola too. I know there will be a debate about Bradley Barcola's end-product but I love watching him in full flow when he is running past defenders - there is no better sight in football than moments like that.

Rio Ngumoha is exciting as well, and he has such a good football brain which makes him even more dangerous.

Everything points to a Liverpool win, but I am hesitant to just go with that because Everton are coming off the back of a drubbing by Brentford . You can imagine David Moyes giving his side a miserable old week and getting stuck into his players.

I didn't think James Tarkowski should have been sent off in that game, but he will be suspended here. It is his absence that swings it for me because he is a real leader for Everton .

Nathan's prediction: Everton are usually the underdogs in this game but both teams are pretty level at the moment. One of our record producers is a huge Liverpool fan so he won't be happy with me... but I am going to say Everton will take it. 2-1

I was at Newcastle 's draw with Arsenal last week and, in fairness to Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle, he changed things around at half-time and got his reward.

Jaissle needed that half of football, because I don't think the Newcastle fans have been too convinced by his approach, but this is another very tough game for him.

Brighton probably still can't believe they lost to Hull last week - but lightning is not going to strike twice.

Nathan's prediction: I have to give a shout out to my statistician Lucy here, because there were a couple of teams I didn't know a lot about and she gave me some good insight. So, Brighton have scored a lot of goals this season and I think they will get more here. 3-1

Thomas Frank has got a huge task at Crystal Palace . They are conceding so many goals.

Losing Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi from their defence was like Robbie Williams and Jason Orange leaving Take That, because they were never going to be the same without them.

I still think Frank has got some decent attacking players, however.

The Hull keeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis, looks like a great signing. I don't know how he made some of his saves against Brighton and he probably doesn't know himself either.

Brighton should have buried them and I think Palace will get plenty of chances too.

Fair play to Hull for their spirit and the way they scrap for each other, but I still think they are going to go down.

Hull fans are probably wondering if I am ever going to predict they will win a game... the answer is no, at least not this week anyway.

Nathan's prediction: Palace have given up 27 goals in 11 games which is a lot. Hull have surprised a few people this season and I am backing them here. 0-2

Bournemouth are on a long winning run in the league but I've been impressed by Fulham whenever I've watched them.

Alvaro Arbeloa's side have not been great at home, with only one win at Craven Cottage so far, so I am going with them to get another draw - which would be their fourth in a row.

Nathan's prediction: Both these teams have picked up a lot, so this is a tough one to call. 2-2

Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi must think a lot of 18-year-old midfielder Luca Williams-Barnett after picking him for their win over Ipswich .

I love to see managers trust young players like that, especially because Spurs have had such a tricky season so far.

It will be interesting to see whether De Zerbi picks him again here, but I feel like the outcome of this game is more dependent on which Sunderland we see.

They picked up a good point at Villa last time out, but they never seem to be quite the same after they have played in Europe, like they are doing this week.

The Black Cats will be without injured duo Brian Brobbey and Granit Xhaka for this game too, so I don't think they will have enough to win it.

Nathan's prediction: Dave Stewart from Eurythmics lives in Nashville too and is a good buddy of mine - and he is Sunderland until death! He is such a die-hard fan that every time we have dinner, we will sit there and talk about 'Haway the Lads' and just shoot the breeze about Sunderland .

So I am going to back them in this one, because of Dave and also because of my neighbour Jeremy, who I mentioned earlier.

Jeremy was especially cocky when they had Harry Kane and he would just talk so much smack - I always knew if they were doing good because I'd get a text from him. So, because Jeremy is such a cocky little Spurs fan, I am saying Sunderland will win. 2-1

I always enjoy this game because of Gabriel's battle with Erling Haaland, but it is in midfield where I think it will be decided.

Manchester City have spent a lot of money on players in that part of the pitch but Enzo Maresca has not found the right combination yet.

Somehow Maresca has got to find a way of nullifying Declan Rice, but that will be very difficult because Rice is just an absolute machine.

You can never rule City out because of Haaland's ability to score goals but the only result I see here is an Arsenal win, and I am going for a classic Gunners scoreline.

Nathan's prediction: This is the big one! It's huge. I feel really good about it, too. Arsenal are riding so high at the moment, I feel like we might catch them snoozing.

I predict Haaland will get two goals, Phil Foden will get one too and we will end up with four. 2-4

After drawing a blank since week two, Chris finally picked up another win in week 11 - and it was his spot-on prediction for Liverpool to thump Manchester United 4-0 that sealed the deal.

That meant he got three correct results, including two exact scores - at Anfield, and Tottenham 's 2-0 win over Ipswich - giving him a total of 90 points.

In a tricky week for predictions, where Liverpool were the only team to start the weekend in the Premier League's top six who won, it was those exact scores that made all the difference.

Chris' guest, undisputed world champion boxer Lauren Price, the BBC readers and AI also all got three correct results.

But the BBC readers were the only ones to also get an exact score - in the Spurs game - giving them 60 points.

Lauren and AI both ended up on 30 points - AI did call Newcastle 's draw with Arsenal correctly, but it was wrong about Bournemouth 's win over Nottingham Forest , which everyone else got right.

Not many of you got that Liverpool -United scoreline correct, either.

From around 27,000 predictions, the most popular scoreline picked was a 2-1 home win and only 570 of you went for 4-0.

"When has AI ever gone for a 4-0?" said Sutton. "That's what the crowd wants. The crowd don't want AI - who wants mathematics?

"The crowd want gut-feeling and instinct. I think I should get 1,000 points for that prediction, because I was brave enough to go for it."

For the first time this season, there were SIX games where no-one made a correct prediction - who thought it was easy?

The biggest shock of the week was Leeds ' 4-1 victory at Stamford Bridge. Again from around 27,000 predictions, more than 3,600 (14%) of you did back Daniel Farke's side to win... but just 11 of you saw that scoreline coming.

"It's a beautiful stadium, and an amazing set-up," he said. "Their practice pitches are better than most college pitches in the US."

Image caption, Followill says it was eye-opening to watch City's boys and girls' teams play when he visited their training campus. "I had no idea how much they put into developing kids from the youngest ages all the way up," he said. "That was probably the most impressive thing for me - to see how many young kids were out there, with the ultimate dream of pulling on that blue shirt one day."

articles.title: Barça y Madrid son los grandes dueños de las redes
articles.standfirst: El club azulgrana es el que más crece en 2026 y el blanco se mantiene líder y cuatro de sus jugadores figuran entre los 10 que más crecen en Instagram
articles.summary: El club azulgrana es el que más crece en 2026 y el blanco se mantiene líder y cuatro de sus jugadores figuran entre los 10 que más crecen en Instagram
articles.body: Al Barcelona le ha salido un año bastantes bueno. En términos deportivos, ha retenido LaLiga y la Supercopa de España. Y a nivel social, ha sido el club que más seguidores ha ganado en Instagram y TikTok. Aun así, sigue mirando al Real Madrid desde abajo, ya que el club blanco es el que cuenta con mayor número de seguidores. Según el informe de Football Benchmark, el Barça sumó 16,4 millones desde el 1 de enero, casi un 8% más, y llegó a 224 millones. El Madrid añadió 12,8, un 5%, y se plantó en 262,2. Los dos viven en otra escala. El Manchester United, tercer club más seguido del fútbol, creció 4,4 millones en el mismo periodo, de modo que el Barça casi cuadruplicó su ritmo y el Madrid casi lo triplicó. La distancia entre ambos era de 42 millones el 1 de enero y hoy es de 38,2. El Barça la ha recortado, pero sigue siendo enorme. La mayor parte de ese crecimiento ha llegado por TikTok, que aportó 12,1 de los 16,4 millones del Barça y 10,4 de los 12,8 del Madrid. Descontada esa red, a Instagram le corresponden 4,3 millones del Barça y 2,4 del Madrid, así que la ventaja azulgrana aparece en las dos plataformas. En el conjunto de los 10 clubes del ranking, TikTok explica en torno al 80% del crecimiento neto. El Atlético de Madrid lo ilustra bien. Su TikTok ganó 5,3 millones de seguidores, lo bastante para tapar un pequeño descenso en Instagram y dejar al club sexto, con 5,2 millones netos, por delante del Manchester City, el United y el Arsenal. En la otra tabla, la del crecimiento porcentual, aparece el Deportivo de La Coruña, que pasó de 0,8 a 1,7 millones de seguidores, un 105% más. Con los jugadores cambia el reparto. De los 10 futbolistas que más seguidores han ganado en Instagram, cuatro juegan en el Madrid. Son Bellingham, Mbappé, Endrick y Cucurella. El Barcelona solo tiene uno, pero está mucho más arriba. Lamine Yamal, tercero con 19,8 millones nuevos, solo tiene por delante a Haaland y a Vozinha, el portero caboverdiano de 40 años que se hizo viral a raíz del debut de su selección contra España en el Mundial. Yamal, Bellingham y Haaland empezaron el año con audiencias muy parecidas, entre 39,8 y 41,6 millones, y a 17 de noviembre los separan casi 20 entre el primero y el último. Buena parte del salto de Haaland llegó durante el Mundial, donde marcó siete goles y llevó a Noruega a los cuartos de final. Yamal ganó ese Mundial con España, se llevó por tercer año consecutivo el premio al mejor jugador joven del Balón de Oro y se sitúa en 59,8 millones. Bellingham, en el año en que Inglaterra alcanzó las semifinales, está en 57,0. El tamaño de los dos tiene un matiz importante: Yamal solo con su cuenta de Instagram y ganó más seguidores que el Barça entero entre Instagram y TikTok, 19,8 millones frente a 16,4. Bellingham, con 15,4, también supera lo que sumó el Madrid, que fueron 12,8. Ambos ganaron más que Cristiano Ronaldo, el jugador más seguido de la plataforma, que añadió 10,7 millones hasta los 681,1. Mbappé llega a 137,1 millones, el cuarto futbolista más seguido de Instagram, tras crecer 8 millones. Justo después en la lista aparece Endrick, con 7,9, a solo 100.000 seguidores de distancia. Hablamos de un jugador que empezó 2026 con 15,4 millones, frente a los 129,2 de Mbappé, y para el que esos 7,9 millones equivalen a más de la mitad de su audiencia de enero. Al francés los 8 le suponen un 6% más. Endrick está en 23,3 millones y ha crecido casi lo mismo que el cuarto futbolista más seguido de la plataforma, un dato que no se esperaba en esta tabla. Los fichajes dejan otra lectura en la tabla de crecimiento porcentual. Entre los diez jugadores cuya audiencia más ha crecido en proporción, el Madrid tiene dos, Diomande y Cucurella, y el Barcelona uno, Gordon. El caso más llamativo es el de Yan Diomande, tercero, con un 2.785% más hasta los 5,2 millones. Por delante solo tiene a Tim Payne y a Vozinha, dos fenómenos virales del Mundial. En 2024 jugaba en la DME Academy, un equipo de Florida en la UPSL. Después pasó por el Leganés y el RB Leipzig, y en agosto llegó al Real Madrid por 125 millones de euros iniciales, más variables. En dos años ha pasado de la UPSL al Madrid, y su cuenta de Instagram ha ido a la par. Anthony Gordon, sexto, pasó de 0,6 a 4,8 millones, un 672% más, en el año de su fichaje por el Barcelona. Cucurella aparece en las dos listas de jugadores, la de seguidores ganados y la de crecimiento porcentual, junto a Vozinha y Michael Olise. Pasó de 2,5 a 9,4 millones, un 282% más, en un año en el que se incorporó al Madrid y ganó el Mundial con España. El Madrid sigue 38,2 millones por delante y el Barcelona crece más deprisa. Cada uno ha incorporado este año a un jugador que empezó 2026 con menos de un millón de seguidores, Diomande y Gordon, y que ya suman 5,2 y 4,8. Los separan más de 50 millones de Bellingham y de Lamine, que están en 57 y 59,8. Queda por ver cuánto de ese trecho recortan en 2027.

articles.title: Quique encumbra a Mourinho: "Ha trascendido a todas las modas"
articles.standfirst: Lo comparó con el laureado extécnico de baloncesto Gregg Popovich
articles.summary: Lo comparó con el laureado extécnico de baloncesto Gregg Popovich
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores, preguntado sobre Jose Mourinho, apuntó que es como Gregg Popovich, laureado extécnico de San Antonio Spurs y exseleccionador de Estados Unidos, porque "ha trascendido a todas las modas y tendencias" en el fútbol, en este caso. El preparador albiazul compareció en sala de prensa antes de visitar al Real Madrid, y desveló que recientemente ha leído la autobiografía del reconocido preparador de la NBA, quien como el portugués ha superado los tiempos. "El fútbol ha cambiado tácticamente, físicamente, ofensivamente y defensivamente, y Mourinho sigue siendo competitivo con sus equipos", consideró Quique Sánchez Flores, que tuvo buenas palabras para el entrenador del equipo blanco. "Le tengo mucho cariño", subrayó. "Es un entrenador adaptable a las tendencias, a las modas de los sistemas, las tácticas y el progreso que tiene el propio fútbol, y eso le da la importancia y el nivel que tiene", opinó. "Tenemos que ser un equipo que conceda poco porque nos querrá encontrar las rendijas del sistema, nos va a intentar dominar y tiene muchas herramientas", avisó el técnico madrileño, que puso el foco en "no dejar correr al rival" porque si lo hacen "es un peligro". Sabe que se medirán a un equipo "fuerte y dominante y superior en lo físico y/o técnico", por lo que deben "intentar estar dentro de partido el mayor tiempo posible". Quique Sánchez Flores se mostró convencido de que lo que hicieron ante el Deportivo la pasada jornada les vale "todo" y aunque desveló que le tienta ir a por un planteamiento defensivo, prefiere repetir su planteamiento. "Recuperar pronto, ser agresivos y tener intensidad te vale para todo el tiempo, pero lo que no sirve siempre es dejar unos espacios u otros en función del rival", manifestó. A pesar de que llega una fase ante rivales directos, prefirió centrarse en el próximo partido. "Cada partido es como cada plato, con un sabor diferente y este va a tener otros ingredientes", explicó. "Hay posibilidades", aseguró Sánchez Flores sobre una potencial victoria del conjunto babazorro ante el Real Madrid.

articles.title: FIFA Says It Has Been Victim of a Cyberattack Accessing 'Personal and Business Information'
articles.summary: ZURICH (AP) — FIFA was the victim of a cyberattack that saw hackers gain access to what soccer's world governing body describes as a "limited set of personal and business information," it said Thursday.
articles.body:
ZURICH (AP) — FIFA was the victim of a cyberattack that saw hackers gain access to what soccer's world governing body describes as a "limited set of personal and business information," it said Thursday.

"FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement," the organization said in a statement sent to The Associated Press.

FIFA didn't say when the cyberattack took place, or the precise nature of the hacked information.

Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were FIFA files. Three days later, it appeared to take credit for the hack when responding to a post that said more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been leaked.

"FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data," the governing body said in its statement. "Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned."

The breach comes at a time when FIFA and its president, Gianni Infantino, is under scrutiny after his foiled, secretive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino is also trying to extend his 11-year presidency of FIFA to 2031. He is the favorite when the election is held on March 18, with Kohzo Tashima of Japan and Philippe Diallo of France the other candidates.

articles.title: Carrión no baja el listón pese a la racha: "Tenemos que seguir elevando el nivel"
articles.standfirst: El Leganés buscará ante el Sabadell encadenar tres victorias por primera vez esta temporada
articles.summary: El Leganés buscará ante el Sabadell encadenar tres victorias por primera vez esta temporada
articles.body: Luis Carrión, entrenador del Leganés, se refirió a la racha de dos triunfos consecutivos de su equipo y consideró que deben seguir "elevando el nivel" y exigiéndose para prolongar la buena dinámica en el tiempo, toda vez que cree que están "muy lejos" de llegar a su mejor momento. Todo ello antes de recibir este viernes al Sabadell ante el que buscarán enlazar tres victorias por primera vez en el campeonato. "Cuando estás ganando partidos tenemos que tener la obligación de sentir que nos tienen que hacer mucho muy bien para ganar. Tenemos que seguir elevando el nivel y exigiéndonos para enlazar victorias. Cuando estás en una buena dinámica hay que seguir esforzándote cada día un poco más para conseguir que eso sea largo en el tiempo", dijo. "Estamos en continua mejora, muy lejos de nuestro cien por cien. Creo que casi ningún equipo llega nunca a su cien por cien, porque siempre que llegas a un nivel alto quieres más y puedes más, la verdad. Y nosotros tenemos que mejorar algunas cosas, incidimos en ellas, tenemos los pies en el suelo, queremos crear un modelo de juego que venga bien a nuestros jugadores y a partir de ahí tener opciones", añadió en la rueda de prensa previa al duelo contra el Sabadell. Del rival afirma que le gusta y que ha visto partidos para aprender cosas, sobre todo en lo que se refiere a la presión alta y a situaciones de salida de balón, ponderando igualmente que cuando roba ataca rápido. A los suyos les pide intentar ser estables durante los 90 minutos, pese a que entiende que a veces es complicado, y asegura que aunque mantener la portería a cero "es básico", el potencial ofensivo del equipo a veces les condiciona. "Entiendo que somos un equipo que ofensivamente tenemos potencial, estamos jugando con muchos jugadores de corte ofensivo en el once. Eso hace que muchas veces lleguemos con mucha gente, generemos más situaciones de gol y también que tengamos cierta dificultad a la hora de parar sus ataques, que creo que tenemos que mejorar con las interrupciones en campo rival, en esa primera presión", expresó. Preguntado sobre los jugadores con menos minutos, no ve "tanta distancia entre algunos jugadores que no están jugando y los que están jugando". Y aseguró que "aquí todo el mundo pelea a muerte todas las semanas y eso está muy bien, habla muy bien del grupo. El que trabaje y no decaiga y esté jugando menos tendrá premio, seguro. En muchos partidos la gente que ha salido de banquillo ha acabado mejorando un poco el nivel de lo que había, que eso es lo que yo quiero y por lo que me peleo mucho".

articles.body:
¡Muy buenas tardes! ¡Bienvenidos a la Conference League! ¡Bienvenidos al Iberia 1899-Getafe! En menos de dos horas arranca en el Mikheil Meskhi Stadioni un duelo clave en sus aspiraciones para lograr el pase a la siguiente ronda de la Conference League . Los azulones son conscientes de que tanto el duelo de Georgia como el siguiente frente al Inter d'Escaldes están marcados en rojo para sacar un seis de seis que los ponga en una posición favorable para clasificarse a los dieciseisavos de final tras un mal inicio.

En el capítulo de novedades, Bordalás ha desplazado a 22 futbolistas a Tiflis con la buena noticia de la recuperación de Andrés García tras sus molestias ligueras y la disponibilidad de Nemanja Gudelj , fresco después de cumplir sanción en el campeonato doméstico. Por contra, el técnico alicantino mantiene las bajas por lesión de Abdel Abqar (molestias en la rodilla izquierda), Sebastián Boselli, Juanmi Jiménez y Christantus Uche , además de la de Dani Carvajal , lesionado y no inscrito en la competición continental.

Enfrente estará un FC Iberia 1999 (vigente campeón y actual líder de la liga georgiana) que ocupa la 29.ª plaza con el mismo punto que los getafenses tras sumar unas tablas y dos derrotas --la más reciente por 2-1 ante el FC Copenhague--.

Pese a la distancia, el equipo del sur de Madrid no estará solo en el Mikheil Meskhi de Georgia y una representación de la hinchada alentará a los suyos en la primera de las finales para seguir vivos en competición.

Con estos ingredientes, el Getafeestá obligado a sacar adelante un partido en el que ya no tiene margen de error. Una vez hechas las presentaciones, ¡arrancamos!

articles.title: Just 3 months after moving to US, Indian-origin English footballer Krissh Mahatma, 18, shot dead outside Mississippi restaurant
articles.summary: Indian-origin footballer Krissh Mahatma, just three months into his career in the US, was tragically shot dead outside a Mississippi restaurant after a confrontation. A suspect has been arrested as the community mourns the loss.
articles.body: Krissh Mahatma had moved from London to the United States to pursue a football career and was only three months into his first season with the Co-Lin Wolves when his life was cut short. The 18-year-old striker was shot dead outside a taco restaurant in Jackson, Mississippi, after an argument involving a group of people reportedly escalated into gunfire. A 22-year-old man has since been arrested and charged with murder.Krissh Mahatma shot dead outside Mississippi restaurantMahatma was fatally shot at approximately 3.39am on Sunday outside Green Ghost Tacos, a popular restaurant in downtown Jackson. The establishment was closed at the time, and the shooting reportedly took place in a parking lot across the street as Mahatma and a group of people were leaving the area, according to sources who spoke to local broadcaster WLBT.The London-born footballer had been with teammates from Copiah-Lincoln Community College, where he played for the Co-Lin Wolves. Witnesses told Dark Horse Press that the group noticed an intoxicated man outside the restaurant and offered to give him a lift home. The offer allegedly led to an argument, which escalated into a physical confrontation before the man produced a firearm and fired at the group.Mahatma was struck by a bullet and taken to a nearby hospital in a private vehicle, where he was pronounced dead, according to Hinds County Coroner Jeramiah Howard, as reported by WLBT. The Mississippi Department of Public Safety has not provided further details about what prompted the confrontation.Capitol Police subsequently arrested Danny Luna, 22, and charged him with murder. Police Chief Mark Miller acknowledged the arrest while recognising the loss suffered by Mahatma's family“While this arrest is an important step toward justice, we recognize that nothing can ease the pain of losing a loved one,” Miller said, offering his “thoughts and prayers” to Mahatma's “family and loved ones”.The investigation is ongoing, and the circumstances surrounding the fatal confrontation have not been fully established by authorities.From London football to a new life with the Co-Lin WolvesMahatma was a freshman at Copiah-Lincoln Community College in Wesson, approximately 45 miles south of Jackson. He played as a forward, wore the No. 11 shirt and had joined the college's soccer programme after previously representing Watford 'A' in England's post-16 Community and Education Football Alliance league.Co-Lin announced his signing in February with a graphic welcoming him to the team and the message: “Welcome to the Wolfpack, Krissh.”He had made 14 appearances during his first three months with the Wolves, scoring once. His goal came in September, during a 3-2 victory over National Park College.The college community paid tribute following news of his death, with Co-Lin president Dewayne Middleton expressing the institution's grief.“Copiah-Lincoln Community College is mourning the loss of freshman soccer player Krissh Mahatma. Krissh will be deeply missed by his teammates and the entire Co-Lin family,” Middleton said in a statement.Mahatma had moved across the Atlantic only months earlier to continue his education and develop his football career. His death has left teammates, coaches and those who had welcomed him to the college community mourning a young player whose time in the United States had only just begun.Family, college and restaurant owner respond to tragedyA fundraiser established to support Mahatma's family described the loss of a young man who had left home to begin a new chapter of his life.“He was just beginning a new chapter of life far away from home,” the fundraiser said.“His sudden passing has left his family, friends, teammates, coaches, and the entire Co-Lin soccer community heartbroken.“Behind this tragedy is a family grieving the loss of their son and loved ones trying to make sense of a loss that feels impossible to put into words.”Green Ghost Tacos also issued a statement after the shooting, offering condolences while clarifying that the restaurant was not open or conducting business when the incident occurred. The owner said:“On behalf of the entire Green Ghost family, I extend my deepest and most heartfelt condolences to the family, friends, loved ones, and university community mourning the tragic loss of a young student. Our hearts are heavy, and our thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected by this devastating incident.“While this tragedy occurred near our establishment, we would like to clarify that Green Ghost was closed and was not conducting business at the time of the shooting.“The safety and well-being of our patrons, employees, and surrounding community remain a top priority. We are committed to cooperating fully with law enforcement as they investigate the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident.“Out of respect for the grieving family and the investigation, we will refrain from speculating or commenting further on the details at this time.“Above all, we recognize that a family has suffered an unimaginable loss. We ask that the community join us in extending compassion, prayers, and support to those affected during this incredibly difficult time.”Mahatma's death has left his family grieving in England and his teammates in Mississippi mourning a player who had travelled thousands of miles to pursue his ambitions. He was 18.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: La carambola de la Champions: Bruno se da una 'autoasistencia' gracias al hoyo que él mismo abrió justo antes
articles.standfirst: El portugués anotó el 1-2 con fortuna, con un bote extraño del balón que despistó a Pereira
articles.summary: El portugués anotó el 1-2 con fortuna, con un bote extraño del balón que despistó a Pereira
articles.body: Bruno Fernandes está tan acostumbrado a hacer gol como a dar asistencias. Lo que no es tan normal es que un gol suyo venga precedido por una asistencia también suya, si es que se puede calificar de tal la carambola con la que logró el 1-2 del Manchester United ante el Sporting de Portugal. Obviamente se trata de una carambola y no de algo realizado a propósito por el jugador, pero no deja de tener su gracia. En la jugada previa al gol, Bruno corre al área para intentar cazar un balón que no llega a sus dominios y, al frenar, levanta un poco el césped. La jugada sigue y el balón le vuelve a llegar a Bruno, que se gira y chuta con la zurda con tanta fortuna que el balón va a pegar en ese hoyo que él mismo habría creado segundos antes. El bote extraño despista a Pereira, que no puede detener la pelota tras el brusco cambio de dirección y sólo puede ver cómo el balón entra en su portería.

articles.title: SFA to deliver revised proposal after young player vote delayed
articles.summary: The Scottish FA will continue consulting with SPFL clubs in a bid to get more game time for homegrown talent after initial plans put forward by the governing body failed to reach a member vote.
articles.body:
The Scottish FA says they will continue consulting with SPFL clubs in a bid to get more game time for homegrown talent after initial plans put forward by the governing body failed to reach a member vote.

Following an all-club meeting at St Andrews in September , the SFA proposed financial incentives - and penalties - along with quotas, in a bid to get more youngsters playing for clubs.

Initially, these proposals were to have been voted on at a SFA general meeting in October and the SPFL's annual meeting this month.

But the SFA now say they are aiming to put refreshed proposals to the clubs in the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of the 2027-28 season.

Despite the governing body saying they are "encouraged", they add that "recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation."

"The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews," a Scottish FA statement read.

"We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game."

"It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams."

Craig Mulholland, SFA chief football officer, has engaged with clubs to encourage more playing time for younger players, however media speculation suggests those plans may have been diluted.

At their initial consultation with clubs, they put forward three suggestions to increase minutes for young Scottish players:

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Scottish Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Premier Sports Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Clubs should field Scotland-eligible Under-21 players for an average of 60 minutes in each game across all four SPFL divisions (6% of available minutes).

The proposals were introduced following a dramatic dip in Scottish-born players being played by Premiership clubs and suggestions of a fear by managers and owners to take a chance on academy players.

Statistics also reflect a huge increase in young players being tempted south to club academies in England, prompting widespread concerns they could be lost in a vast youth system rather than breaking into first teams domestically.

"Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right," the governing body adds.

articles.title: España se instala en el nirvana
articles.standfirst: La selección, con goles de Tunkara y Trujillano, supera con autoridad a Marruecos (0-2) y avanza como primera de grupo a dieciseisavos de final del Mundial Sub-17
articles.summary: La selección, con goles de Tunkara y Trujillano, supera con autoridad a Marruecos (0-2) y avanza como primera de grupo a dieciseisavos de final del Mundial Sub-17
articles.body: Da gusto verlos jugar. Hay algo en esta España que convierte cada partido en una demostración de fútbol. Y cada victoria en una invitación a imaginar lo que todavía está por venir. Los de David Cubillo siguen recorriendo la alfombra roja de Doha sin que nadie consiga hacerles tropezar. Ni siquiera Marruecos (0-2), que prometía ser el primer examen serio y terminó rindiéndose a la superioridad de una selección que parece tenerlo todo bajo control. Tunkara puso el talento y Trujillano, en la segunda parte, el instinto del goleador para sellar el pleno de victorias y asegurar el liderato del grupo. España entra en los dieciseisavos con 22 goles a favor, ninguno en contra y una autoridad intimidante. Cubillo volvió a mover las piezas después del aluvión de rotaciones ante Fiyi. Guille Ponce, el único futbolista que todavía no había debutado en el Mundial, encontró por fin su oportunidad bajo los palos. Yeremaiah también se estrenó como titular en la punta del ataque, mientras Rafa Cruz, Roberto Tomás y Trujillano, los hombres que habían acaparado los goles de la jornada anterior, esperaban su turno en el banquillo. Al otro lado, Marruecos prescindió de inicio de Ibrahim Rabbaj, el 'Messi marroquí', reservado para la segunda mitad. Sus aficionados, en cambio, no se guardaron nada. Más de 300 seguidores, un tambor y un "Dima Maghreb" que resonaba por encima del resto de voces. La grada tenía dueño antes de que empezara el partido. Sobre el césped, Marruecos quiso imponer desde el principio una autoridad más física que futbolística. Mayans y Tunkara recibieron los primeros recados. Hubo poco espacio para la cortesía y todavía menos para detenerse a pensar. España avisó con una combinación entre Sobral, Yeremaiah, Tunkara e Ïu Martínez, pero fue Sergi Mayans quien encontró la forma de desmontar el entramado marroquí. Desde la defensa, el central sacó el catalejo y puso un balón a la espalda de la zaga que parecía llevar escrita la dirección de Tunkara. El 10 había leído el pase antes de que saliera de sus botas. Controló para orientarse y resolvió con la zurda. Dos toques. Los suficientes para inaugurar el marcador antes del minuto veinte. A partir de entonces, cada intervención de Tunkara pareció convertirse en un asunto personal para los futbolistas marroquíes. Lo buscaron con insistencia, aunque no precisamente para quitarle la pelota de manera limpia. Laarej terminó viendo la amarilla por una de las entradas más duras. En una acción, el azulgrana dejó atrás a tres defensores y encontró a Yeremaiah completamente solo ante la portería. Le había hecho prácticamente todo el trabajo, pero el delantero madridista se topó con el pie del guardameta cuando ya parecía inevitable el segundo. El descanso permitió a Cubillo modificar el ataque. Trujillano sustituyó a Yeremaiah y Marruecos recurrió poco después a Rabbaj, consciente de que necesitaba algo distinto para discutirle el partido a España. Pero el talento del Chelsea apenas encontró espacios para intervenir. Quien sí los encontró fue Eloi Gómez. En el minuto 61, el centrocampista recibió cerca de la frontal y, con un toque, descubrió a Trujillano dentro del área. El delantero del Atlético hizo lo que llevan toda la vida haciendo los buenos nueves: orientarse hacia la portería y resolver antes de que el defensor pudiera reaccionar. Un zurdazo para el segundo. Marruecos pidió revisar un posible fuera de juego, pero el FVS confirmó que estaba habilitado. El gol era legal y el primer puesto respiraba tranquilo. Hasta entonces, Guille Ponce había contemplado buena parte del encuentro desde la distancia. Marruecos apenas había encontrado la manera de acercarse a su portería, aunque terminó obligándolo a justificar su titularidad. Hadidi ejecutó una falta desde el balcón del área y el madridista reaccionó con una velocidad extraordinaria para desviar el balón. Le quedó a España algún intento tímido, ya con Roberto Tomás y Rafa Cruz sobre el césped. Marruecos, obligada por el marcador, buscó una reacción que nunca terminó por oler. Se acercó algo más al área española, pero acabó resignada a la autoridad de un equipo que manejó los tiempos y apenas dejó asomarse a la sorpresa. Los de Cubillo se instalan en el nirvana. Y, por ahora, nadie parece capaz de sacarlos de allí.
