articles.title: Jude Bellingham hailed for ‘absolute class act’ after stopping male journalist from interrupting female reporter in chaotic Real Madrid interview
articles.summary: Jude Bellingham impresses fans by standing up for BBC journalist Elizabeth Conway during a chaotic post-match interview following Real Madrid's Champions League victory, highlighting the challenges female reporters face in sports journalism.
articles.body: Jude Bellingham had just scored what he described as the best goal of his life, but one of his most widely praised moments after Real Madrid's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV had nothing to do with football. The England midfielder stopped a male reporter from interrupting BBC journalist Elizabeth Conway, insisting she be allowed to finish her question in a crowded mixed zone at the Bernabeu.Bellingham steps in after BBC reporter is interruptedBellingham was in considerable demand after coming off the bench to help Real Madrid beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday. His outstanding volley had put Madrid ahead, while he later provided the assist for Vinicius Jr's fifth goal, giving reporters plenty to ask about after the final whistle.BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway was among those waiting to speak to the midfielder in the mixed zone, where journalists gather behind a barrier to interview players as they leave the pitch. She had asked Bellingham about the goal when another reporter interrupted her attempt to ask a second question.Bellingham immediately intervened.“Sorry, she's got one more,” he said, pointing towards Conway and making clear that she should be allowed to continue.The journalist then asked whether Bellingham felt he was playing the best football of his career for both club and country.“My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn't really matter,” he replied.“Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.”Conway later shared the exchange on Instagram, writing: “Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,” alongside a handshake emoji. The clip quickly circulated online, with supporters praising the midfielder for his consideration.BBC presenter Kelly Somers was among those who responded, writing: “So lovely he did this to you @elizabeth.conway_ and well done for also standing your ground.”The BBC Football account also joined in, joking: “Jude Bellingham with his second assist of the night.”Elizabeth Conway explains the pressure of interviewing at Real MadridConway subsequently discussed the incident on BBC Radio WM, explaining why Bellingham's intervention meant so much in an environment she described as intimidating.The mixed zone at the Bernabeu can become particularly chaotic when a high-profile player stops to speak to the media. Journalists compete for space around the barrier, with microphones, cameras and reporters often crowding one another in an effort to secure an interview.“It is utter carnage,” Conway said.“Obviously as an English reporter at Real Madrid, getting Jude is exactly what we want, it's gold dust.“You've got elbows you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you.“I'm one of very, very, few female reporters and one of very, very, few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so important.”Conway explained that interruptions were commonplace and that reporters were expected to compete aggressively for the opportunity to ask questions. In a separate video shared online, she described how being shorter than many of the journalists around her meant she needed to position herself directly at the front of the barrier.“Because I’m short, I have to get right at the front of the barrier to have any chance. I was right at the front underneath Jude’s chin,” she said.“It’s normal protocol, at least at Real Madrid, that journalists just throw in questions. There are no niceties or politeness; it’s everyone out for themselves.”She particularly appreciated that Bellingham had noticed the interruption and deliberately made room for her to continue.“It was so nice,” she said, adding that the gesture showed him being “respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist”.“It was especially appreciated because I am one of so few female journalists at Real Madrid, and one of the very few English journalists,” she added.Bellingham's stunning goal earns praise from Mourinho and ValverdeThe exchange came after a performance that had already made Bellingham the centre of attention at the Bernabeu. Introduced from the bench, the 23-year-old produced a remarkable finish to put Real Madrid in front against PSV.After collecting a loose ball around 25 yards from goal, he controlled it with his left foot before flicking it into the air with his right and striking a volley with the outside of the same boot. The ball flew into the far corner, leaving PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar with little chance.Bellingham was asked what had gone through his mind during the finish.“Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,” he said. “I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through.“It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it.“It was a nice goal and important for the team being the second goal and gave us control.”He was even more emphatic when asked to rank the strike among his previous goals.“I think this was the best goal of my life,” he declared.Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho was equally impressed, explaining how Bellingham had changed the team's performance after his introduction.“Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,” Mourinho said. “He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.”Bellingham's brother Jobe, meanwhile, had his own reaction to the goal after featuring for Borussia Dortmund in their 1-1 draw against Arsenal on the same evening. He jokingly suggested the shot had “come off his shin” before conceding that it was a “great goal”.The performance also came amid growing attention over Bellingham's future at Real Madrid. Daily Mail Sport reported on November 24 that the England international was in advanced discussions over a contract extension until 2031, with negotiations having begun in September.His existing deal runs until 2029 and is understood to be worth approximately £12.5 million a year after tax. Madrid are keen to reward his performances with improved terms, potentially bringing his salary in line with team-mate Vinicius Jr, whose contract extension last summer was reportedly worth around £500,000 a week after tax.Sources at the Spanish club were said to be confident that an agreement was approaching. For now, however, Bellingham's intervention in the mixed zone has given supporters another reason to praise a player whose influence on the night extended well beyond his remarkable goal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Latest Heisman Watch Odds and 2026 Race Predictions Entering Week 13
articles.summary: Oddsmakers seem convinced that the Heisman Trophy race is already finished.
articles.body:
Oddsmakers seem convinced that the Heisman Trophy race is already finished.

Could Week 13 of the college football season have anything to say about that?

After laying out the latest Heisman Trophy odds, we'll spotlight what to watch in Week 13 and then decide if it will have an impact by crowning a predicted winner.

There will be a bunch of great football action this weekend. Very little of it will impact the Heisman race, though.

Darian Mensah might have made things interesting with a ferocious finish, but his Week 12 dud (241 yards passing, no touchdowns, two interceptions) probably torpedoed his candidacy. It might be the same story for CJ Carr, who tossed two of his three interceptions this season over his last two outings. They'll close against Boston College and at Syracuse, respectively.

Gio Lopez is trending the other way, though, and might have a chance to secure his spot as a finalist. He has four rushing touchdowns and three passing scores over the past two weeks, and his lone interception this season came during his club's only loss: back in the middle of September against Miami. He'll finish the regular season with a visit from Duke.

Really, though, all eyes are on Jeremiah Smith and Devon Dampier. Because if there is still a Heisman race left, it's down to these two.

Smith has been unstoppable this season, and he had Ohio State largely appearing the same before his quarterback, Julian Sayin, hurt his throwing arm in mid-October. That injury derailed the Buckeyes, but Smith is still posting absurd numbers (five touchdown catches in the four games Sayin has missed).

Smith never struggles to snag the spotlight, but he could have extra attention on him in the always spirited rivalry game with Michigan.

As for Dampier, he'll be aiming to put the finishing touches on a perfect regular season with his Utes carrying an 11-0 record into a home game with West Virginia. Dampier, who has thrown and rushed for multiple scores in three consecutive contests, could post the kind of stat line that at least makers voters think twice.

...Smith. Come on, did you expect anything different?

All the credit in the world goes to Dampier. He's been special this season, and so have his Utes. He should be the clear and unquestioned silver medalist.

But Smith is just different—outstanding in the very way this award is meant to recognize. He has a touchdown in all but one game played so far, and that was a 56-point thrashing that might've been even more lopsided than that. He has nearly twice as many games with 100-plus receiving yards (seven) as not (four).

He still needs to produce in the finale, and he shouldn't take Dampier's candidacy lightly. But everything we've seen suggests Smith has another big outing in store, and this one might be the clincher.

articles.title: Laura Freigang: Germany forward banned for missing drugs tests
articles.summary: Germany international Laura Freigang is suspended from football for 16 months over issues relating to three drugs tests.
articles.body:
Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests.

The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027.

The 16-month suspension begins from the date of notification by the German Football Association (DFB), which took place in June.

The World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the National Anti-Doping Agency (Nada), DFB and Freigang reached a dispute resolution agreement.

The dispute said Entracht Frankfurt forward Freigang committed three reporting and/or testing failures between 11 March 2025 and 23 February 2026.

Freigang can return to training two months prior to the end of the suspension period but cannot play matches until after 7 October.

All personal records of appearances, goals, assists or other statistics from 23 February 2026 are nullified, though Frankfurt's results are unaffected.

This season Freigang has scored six goals and provided two assists in 11 starts in the Frauen-Bundesliga.

Since joining the club in 2020, the striker has scored 107 goals in 187 appearances and was in the Germany squad for October's friendly victories over Australia and Japan.

In a club statement , external , Franfurt said they will "begin discussions shortly to determine the terms of her future employment relationship".

Freigang's current contract is due to expire on 30 June 2027.

Frankfurt's director of women's football Katharina Kiel said: "The agreement now reached provides clarity and planning security in a process unprecedented for Eintracht Frankfurt - for us as a club, but above all for Laura.

"The way she and the team have handled the situation in recent months, and how Laura personally led by example with her performance on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the highest recognition.

"The identified shortcomings, despite the agreement to settle the dispute, have resulted in a suspension, which means the loss of a key player."

articles.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin: Leeds United striker signs new contract until 2029
articles.summary: England international Dominic Calvert-Lewin signs a new contract to stay with Leeds United until 2029.
articles.body:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract to stay with Leeds United until 2029.

The former Everton striker, 29, has five goals and one assist so far in the Premier League this season, with Daniel Farke's side sitting seventh in the table.

Confirmation of Calvert-Lewin's deal follows speculation about his future at the club, with reports that he was interesting Manchester United .

Calvert-Lewin scored 15 goals across all competitions during his first season at Elland Road after joining in August 2025, and the form earned him an England recall in March.

He was also called up by Thomas Tuchel this autumn and came off the bench in England's wins against Czech Republic and Spain.

articles.title: La paradoja de la 'Hypertensión': los tres equipos con mejor puntería no están entre los primeros
articles.standfirst: Los datos de Valladolid, Celta Fortuna y Eibar demuestran la locura de nuestra División de Plata
articles.summary: Los datos de Valladolid, Celta Fortuna y Eibar demuestran la locura de nuestra División de Plata
articles.body: Para entender la categoría de plata hay que separar la calidad técnica del remate y la eficacia competitiva global. Y es que ambos conceptos no suelen venir de la mano. Disparar entre tres palos con precisión es valioso pero, en la 'Hypertensión', como popularmente se conoce a nuestra Segunda división por casos como éste, los partidos se deciden por el balance entre las dos áreas y por la capacidad de sostener ventajas en escenarios cerrados. La clasificación general responde a quién suma puntos y compite arriba, mientras que la tabla de precisión explica quién dirige mejor sus tiros a puerta. Basándonos en ésta última observamos que, tras 15 jornadas, aunque hay seis equipos con un partido menos, la racha de acierto o el bloqueo del conjunto rival puede distorsionar con facilidad los porcentajes, pero es innegable que tener buen disparo no salva a un equipo si concede facilidades atrás. El Real Valladolid (primero en tiros a puerta con un 41,41% de acierto) es el equipo que mejor dirige sus disparos hacia la portería rival y marca 1,47 goles por partido (con 2,8 participaciones directas de gol o asistencia por encuentro), pero ocupa el 14º lugar en la clasificación. Aprovecha 0,27 goles por tiro -una cifra más baja que los equipos de arriba- y, sobre todo, recibe 22 goles en 15 jornadas (+1 de diferencia de goles), lo que resta valor a su buen disparo. El Celta Fortuna (segundo en tiros a puerta, con un 40,7 %) es la prueba de que la puntería por sí sola no basta para estar arriba: es segundo en disparos a portería, pero está el 18º en la tabla con 14 puntos. Con 1,27 goles por partido, 2 acciones de gol o asistencia por encuentro y 0,27 goles por disparo, crea menos peligro que los líderes y sufre mucho atrás (27 goles encajados en 15 partidos, -7 de diferencia de goles). Y luego está el Eibar, tercero en tiros a puerta, con 39,46 %, y único de estos tres que pelea cerca de la zona alta (es séptimo con 24 puntos y un partido menos). Une una gran puntería (39,46 %) con un ataque dinámico (23 goles, 1,57 goles por partido, 2,79 goles más asistencias por partido y 0,3 goles por tiro), aunque los 17 goles recibidos (+6 de diferencia de goles) le mantienen justo fuera de los puestos de los 'playoffs'. En resumen, en la División de Plata afinar los disparos es solo una pieza del puzle, sobre todo si no va acompañado de un equilibrio defensivo y una continuidad competitiva. Y así resulta muy curioso que, a día de hoy, ninguno de los tres clubes con más puntería de la categoría ocuparían siquiera plaza de 'playoffs'.

articles.title: England Under-21s: Lee Carsley urges Young Lions to make history at Euro 2027
articles.summary: England have won the past two European Under-21 Championships, and Lee Carsley says they will "go all out" for a hat-trick.
articles.body:
Lee Carsley has urged his England Under-21s to create a legacy as they aim for a third straight European title.

The Young Lions - who have won the past two European Championships in 2023 and 2025 under Carsley - have been drawn in Group A against France, Poland and co-hosts Serbia at Euro 2027.

Only Italy have won three successive European Under-21 tournaments - between 1992 and 1996 - but that was when just eight teams competed at the finals and not the current 16.

Head coach Carsley told BBC Sport: "The players I am privileged to coach and work with have a great opportunity to make history with three in a row in this format and create their own legacy within the under-21s."

He was speaking after Thursday's draw in Belgrade, with Serbia hosting the tournament with Albania.

"This group of players are in a really unique position and it will be a while before another group will be in this position," said Carsley.

"Let's go for it. Why not? Go all out to try to win it. That's what we're going to do. We have the players who can do that.

"They are highly motivated. We have seen that in the last two tournaments we have had, the players were so determined to win every game and it makes it a lot easier from a coaching point of view."

England will open their campaign against France - who they beat 3-2 in Bristol last week - on 16 June in Leskovac before facing Serbia in Belgrade on 19 June.

The Young Lions stay in the Serbian capital for their final group game against Poland on Tuesday, 22 June.

articles.title: Hutchinson evita que Imanol meta en un lío al Milan
articles.standfirst: Comandó la remontada contra Olympiacos con un gol y dos asistencias
articles.summary: Comandó la remontada contra Olympiacos con un gol y dos asistencias
articles.body: El Olympiacos de Mendilibar apenas había encajado un gol en las cuatro primeras jornadas de esta Europa League y arrancó ganando 2-0 ante un Milan que se estaba metiendo en serios problemas para avanzar a las rondas eliminatorias. En la segunda parte, sin embargo, Omari Hutchinson firmó una auténtica exhibición —un gol y dos asistencias— para remontar el choque. Moreira sentenció en el descuento. Rúben Amorim, como suele ser habitual en Europa League, dio descanso a Luka Modric. Por lo demás, eso sí, el Milan presentó un once bastante reconocible donde Maignan regresaba bajo palos tras cumplir sanción ante el Ferencvaros. Estupiñán ocupó el carril izquierdo por la baja de Bartesaghi. Alpha Cissé y Jashari probaron fortuna con dos disparos lejanos nada más arrancar el encuentro que, sin embargo, no obligaron a intervenir a Stefan Ortega. Dominaba el balón el Milan... pero se descosía cada vez que perdía el balón. Cumplida la hora de partido, Gustavo Sá botó un saque de esquina cabeceado al fondo de la red por un Lorenzo Pirola que le ganó la posición a De Winter y Diawara. Estaba en todas el central italiano. Escasos minutos después, evitó sobre la línea que Cissé devolviese el empate al marcador tras lograr superar a Stefan Ortega. Ya en el tiempo de descuento de la primera parte, además, volvió a aparecer por el área rival y mandó a las nubes un envío atrás por parte de Gelson Martins. Amorim estaba obligado a intervenir al descanso. Dejó en el banquillo a Estupiñán y Gonçalo Ramos para dar entrada a Musah y Pulisic. Diego Moreira se desplazó al carril izquierdo y fue Cissé quien pasó a ser la referencia del Milan. Nada más regresar de vestuarios, sin embargo, Jota Silva castigó un error en construcción 'fusilando' a Maignan. El Milan caminaba sobre el alambre... pero Hutchinson entró en trance para, en poco más de un cuarto de hora, darle la vuelta al encuentro. En el 56', salió como una 'flecha' desde campo propio y ajustó su remate desde la frontal. En el 63', puso un centro que, con ayuda de Stefan Ortega, Cissé mandó a guardar de cabeza en el segundo palo y, en el 71', desbordó por derecha para volver a asistir a un Pulisic que la clavó de 'tijera'. Llegó a reclamar un penalti Olympiacos en la recta final del encuentro. Pero, ya en el tiempo de descuento, el propio Hutchinson inició una contra que no desperdició el Milan para terminar de sentenciar. Cabalgó Pulisic por el costado izquierdo y habilitó a un Diego Moreira que, tras dejar sentado a su par, resolvió ante Stefan Ortega. El Benfica contaba sus partidos por victorias en esta fase liga de la Europa League. Su clasificación no parece correr ningún peligro. Sin embargo, 'patinaron' a su paso por Plzen... y se volvieron para casa con un contundente 4-0 en contra. En la primera parte, Hrosovsky, Kwabena y Kabongo castigaron con dureza tres errores groseros en salida de balón y, nada más volver del descanso, el propio Kabongo cerró la goleada. Mucho mejor le fue a Carles Martínez Novell y su Bayer Leverkusen en su visita al Dinamo Zagreb (0-2). Todo se puso de cara a los 10' cuando Tillman recogió un balón suelto en el área tras un saque de esquina servido por Aleix García. Justo antes del descanso, el ex del Girona abrió sobre el costado derecho y Quansah, previo recorte dentro del área, resolvió con la zurda al palo corto. También volvió a ganar el Olympique de Marsella por segunda jornada consecutiva después de arrancar la edición con tres derrotas en los tres primeros partidos. Resolvió por la mínima ante el Levski Sofía de Julio Velázquez (1-0) gracias a un penalti transformado por un Amine Gouiri que, eso sí, falló otro a lo 'panenka' después del descanso.

articles.title: ‘Cucho’ Hernández entra al XI ideal de la Champions tras su doblete con el Betis
articles.standfirst: El colombiano fue una de las figuras de la jornada con su dos goles ante el Slovan Bratislava
articles.summary: El colombiano fue una de las figuras de la jornada con su dos goles ante el Slovan Bratislava
articles.body: Juan Camilo 'Cucho' Hernández volvió a demostrar por qué es uno de los delanteros colombianos más importantes del fútbol europeo. Tras varias semanas alejado de las canchas por una lesión, el atacante del Real Betis regresó con un doblete decisivo ante el Slovan Bratislava, fue figura en la victoria 0-2 de su equipo y consiguió un lugar en el XI ideal de la quinta jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions League. El reconocimiento llega en un momento clave para el Betis, que aseguró matemáticamente su continuidad en la competición y ahora pelea por entrar directamente a los octavos de final, evitando así la ronda de playoffs. Cucho no jugaba desde mediados de octubre, cuando el Real Betis cayó 5-2 ante el Barcelona. Su ausencia dejó una baja importante en el ataque verdiblanco, precisamente porque el colombiano había llegado a la temporada con un ritmo goleador destacado. Su regreso no pudo ser mejor. En el Tehelné Pole Stadion, el delantero colombiano anotó dos goles que sellaron la victoria del Betis por 0-2 frente al Slovan Bratislava. El doblete no solo dio tres puntos fundamentales al conjunto español, sino que elevó su cuenta personal a cinco tantos en la actual temporada. Antes de la lesión, Cucho ya había dejado su huella en la Champions: le marcó al Porto en el triunfo 3-2 del Betis. Ahora, con el doblete ante el Slovan, consolidó su presencia como una de las referencias ofensivas del equipo de Manuel Pellegrini en el torneo continental. La UEFA incluyó a Cucho Hernández en el equipo ideal de la quinta jornada, un once integrado por jugadores de alto nivel de distintos clubes europeos. El colombiano compartió delantera con Kylian Mbappé, del Real Madrid, y apareció junto a nombres como Jude Bellingham, Alisson Becker, Nicolò Barella y Anthony Gordon. El XI ideal quedó conformado así: Alisson Becker (Liverpool) Nathan Ngoy (Lille) Logan Costa (Villarreal) Mario Hermoso (Roma) Rayan Cherki (Manchester City) Nicolò Barella (Inter) Luis Milla (Como) Anthony Gordon (Barcelona) Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid) Cucho Hernández (Real Betis) Kylian Mbappé (Real Madrid) Para un futbolista colombiano, entrar en este tipo de selección tiene un valor especial. No solo premia la actuación individual de una jornada, sino que lo coloca en la conversación junto a algunas de las grandes figuras del fútbol mundial. En el caso de Cucho, el doblete fue la evidencia más clara de su impacto: dos goles, una victoria y la clasificación asegurada para su equipo. La victoria ante el Slovan Bratislava tuvo una importancia doble para el Real Betis. Por un lado, aseguró su permanencia en la Champions League; por otro, mantuvo vivas sus opciones de terminar entre los ocho primeros de la fase de liga, posición que permitiría acceder directamente a octavos de final sin pasar por los playoffs. Tras la quinta jornada, el Betis ocupa la sexta posición de la tabla. El objetivo inmediato del club es conservar ese lugar o incluso mejorararlo en los tres compromisos restantes de la fase de liga. Los rivales que quedan son exigentes: Como, Arsenal y Bayern Múnich. El Betis recibirá a Como y Arsenal en casa, mientras que visitará al Bayern en la última jornada. Sumar puntos ante esos equipos será determinante para definir si el conjunto verdiblanco evita la ronda de playoffs. El regreso de Cucho Hernández representa mucho más que la vuelta de un goleador. Para el Betis, significa recuperar a un delantero capaz de resolver partidos, generar peligro constante y aportar experiencia en competiciones de alto nivel. Su doblete ante el Slovan Bratislava llegó en un momento en que el equipo necesitaba resultados y confianza. Además, el rendimiento del colombiano puede cambiar la dinámica ofensiva del Betis de cara al tramo final de la fase de liga europea y al resto de la temporada. Junto a Cucho, el Betis también cuenta con Nelson Deossa, otro colombiano que forma parte del proyecto. La presencia de ambos jugadores le da al equipo una identidad sudamericana relevante y aumenta la atención del público colombiano sobre el rendimiento del club en Europa.

articles.title: Giráldez: “Hemos dejado de jugar con el cerebro y así es difícil”
articles.standfirst: El técnico lamenta otra ocasión perdida
articles.summary: El técnico lamenta otra ocasión perdida
articles.body: Más dolido que en otras partidos de Europa League se mostró Claudio Giráldez, confiando en que los marcadores lleguen para poder seguir adelante en el torneo. Nueva ocasión perdida: “Nos está costando atacar o jugar en superioridad numérica. Sin embargo, creo que hemos sacado muy buenos resultados jugando con uno menos. La explicación es muy sencilla: para jugar al fútbol hay que estar estable, hay que estar tranquilo, hay que asumir la responsabilidad y el favoritismo cuando toca y no somos un equipo preparado ahora mismo para asumirlo. Siempre que el viento se pone demasiado a favor nos entra un exceso de responsabilidad que no debería”. Mejor once contra once: “Hemos hecho un partido en igualdad numérica espectacular, no han llegado al área, hemos tenido varias ocasiones para irnos por delante y los primeros minutos de la superioridad también hemos tenido ocasiones. Luego hemos vuelto a caer en la trampa de la 2ª parte de irnos a contactos, a campos pequeños, de regalarles faltas, de atacar demasiado rápido, de darle vueltas a la pelota y cuando se la quieres dar vas perdiendo y estás en el minuto 85... Cerebro, cabeza, inteligencia, jugar igual de tácticos que somos cuando estamos once contra once creo que es la clave". Lo que les dijo a sus jugadores al descanso: “Evidentemente mi charla o se entendió al revés o me equivoqué en lo que dije porque no arrancamos bien. Nos hacen un gol y ahí entran todos los fantasmas de la dinámica en la que estás a diferencia de la dinámica del rival. También es muy importante para afrontar esos momentos del partido de incertidumbre en los que está en el aire. Hemos regalado dos faltas, te embotellan, es un equipo super físico. Sabemos que un equipo tan físico tiene capacidad de hacerte daño en balón parado, en centro lateral. Hemos dejado de jugar con el cerebro. Cuando juegas sin el cerebro es difícil. Estoy enfadado por cómo hemos actuado en la segunda parte. Es lo que me molesta”.

articles.title: Torreense 1-2 Celtic: Camilo Duran comes off bench to score late winner and keep Hoops' Europa League hopes alive
articles.summary: Report from the Europa League clash between Torreense and Celtic at Campo Manuel Marques; Javi Vazquez' own-goal put Celtic in front; Dany Jean levelled before the break; substitute Camilo Duran headed in a late winner for the Hoops; Martin O'Neill's side are up to 25th
articles.body:
The Colombian striker peeled away to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest, guiding a downward header into the net in the 85th minute.

Duran's 15th goal of the season secured a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and moved Celtic on to six points in the Europa League. His latest decisive contribution follows a match-winning double off the bench in the Hoops' comeback victory over Besiktas last time out.

Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vazquez turned Jota's cross into his own net, with Yang Hyun-jun lurking behind him.

However, the Portuguese Cup winners hit back 10 minutes later after some hesitant defending from the visitors. Alex Alfaro rattled the crossbar with a 22-yard effort, but neither Kieran Tierney nor Colby Donovan could deal with the resulting loose balls, allowing Haiti international Dany Jean to volley home the equaliser.

Celtic dominated possession after the break but struggled to create clear-cut opportunities until Duran's late intervention secured all three points.

The Hoops' attention now turns to Hearts on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, as they look to remain top of the Scottish Premiership.

Their next Europa League match is away to Omonia Nicosia on December 10.

2: CLOSE! Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain sends in a corner, it's flicked on by Liam Scales but Hyun-jun Yang can't knock the ball in before it's cleared.

9: GOAL CELTIC! Javi Vazquez tries to clear Jota's cross but turns it into his own net.

19: GOAL TORREENSE! Alex Alfaro's effort rattles the underside of the bar, Celtic fail to make a clearance and Dany Jean fires in the equaliser.

33: SAVE! Jota's powerful strike is pushed over the bar by Adriel.

36: OFF THE LINE! More awful defending from Celtic, but Liam Scales manages to head the ball clear.

47: SAVE! Jota tries to chip the ball over the goalkeeper but he manages to pluck the ball out of the air.

53: BLOCK! Jota is continuing to cause problems for the hosts as he sends in a cross for Kieran Tierney, which is headed behind.

61: CLOSE! Jean looks to squeeze in a shot at the near post, but it's just wide.

69: CHANCE! A misplaced pass from Oliver Sorensen lets Musa Drammeh get a shot away. Thankfully for Celtic it's wide.

70: LET OFF FOR CELTIC! Trouble at the back again gives Drammeh space to get a shot away, but the former Hearts striker is inches wide.

84: GOAL CELTIC! Camilo Duran rises at the back post to head in James Forrest's cross. Celtic are back ahead.

O'Neill: 'From an almost impossible position, we have hope'

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill on TNT Sports:

"I'm just delighted to have won, it keeps us going if nothing else. We've got six points on the board and we've still a couple of games to go.

"From an almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we've given ourselves some hope.

"Three points tonight were of vital importance. There's lots we can still do to improve our game."

Asked about Camilo Duran, he added: "He's just a magnificent footballer.

"15 goals and we're not into December, he's been flying. He's a terrific player, and that's two games he's come up big for us."

Jota 'enjoying life' as he returns to best

Celtic winger Jota speaking to TNT Sports after his first European appearance for almost two years:

"It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible.

"Right now, it's all about enjoying life. No expectations, just be professional and having the responsibility of being a Celtic player.

"It wasn't easy. I think we just had to stick with our plan and in the end it worked out, that's the most important thing.

"We must believe [Celtic can qualify]. Every game is a different battle, we know what to do."

articles.title: La Juventus se repone a un reestreno para olvidar de Neto
articles.standfirst: Los goles de Cambiaso y Ekhator antes del descanso le dieron la vuelta al choque contra el Omonia Nicosia... mientras que Conceiçao y Boga sentenciaron en la segunda parte
articles.summary: Los goles de Cambiaso y Ekhator antes del descanso le dieron la vuelta al choque contra el Omonia Nicosia... mientras que Conceiçao y Boga sentenciaron en la segunda parte
articles.body: Con la temporada ya iniciada, la Juventus contrató a Neto -se encontraba libre tras acabar contrato con Botafogo- por la grave lesión de Grabara. Se reestreno estuvo lejos de ser idílico. Los goles de Cambiaso y Ekhator antes del descanso, sin embargo, le dieron la vuelta al choque contra el Omonia Nicosia (1-4) antes del descanso, mientras que Conceiçao y Boga resolvieron en la segunda parte. Siguen invictos en esta Europa League y asentados en el Top-8. El veterano guardameta brasileño fue una de las muchas novedades introducidas por Spalletti. También participaron de inicio Gatti, Pape Sarr, Cambiaso, Boga o Ekhator. También un Francisco Conceiçao que volvió a participar después más de un mes ausente por lesión. Suyo, de hecho, fue el primer remate del partido. No salió a especular una Juventus que quería dejar los deberes hechos desde primera hora. De hecho, lanzó la presión más arriba y, sobre todo, de forma más agresiva de lo habitual. En una de sus primeras salidas, sin embargo, el Omonia Nicosia forzó un córner servido por Tankovic y cabeceado por Satka aprovechando una salida en falso de Neto. Se le notó la inactividad. Tuvo acercamientos el Omonia Nicosia como para duplicar la ventaja. A menos de 10' para el descanso, sin embargo, la Juventus consiguió remontar el choque y devolver la tranquilidad a las gradas del Allianz Stadium. En el 37', Cambiaso trazó la diagonal hacia dentro y puso el balón en la escuadra con la zurda. En el 43', trazaron un ataque rápido resuelto por Ekhator a pase de Conceiçao. Primer gol del joven ariete italiano con la 'Vecchia Signora'. A pesar de haberle dado la vuelta al partido, Spalletti retiró a Cabal, perfil más conservador, para dar entrada a Celik. Se acostó en el carril derecho y Cambiaso se cambió a banda izquierda. Volvió a salir con intensidad la Juventus. No quería sustos y obligó a Kaminski a realizar varias intervenciones en los primeros compases de la segunda parte. Metió más madera Spalletti con Koopmeiners, McKennie y Woltemade. Fue Conceiçao, sin embargo, quien terminó de sentenciar el triunfo para la Juventus. Recogió un balón suelto en el sector derecho del área y resolvió mano a mano. Todavía, eso sí, quedaba tiempo para un gol de Boga, que lo había buscando con insistencia durante todo el choque y lo consiguió con otro 'latigazo' a la escuadra. Carlos Vicens debutó como nuevo entrenador del Olympique de Lyon con una meritoria victoria contra el Lille en Ligue 1. Su estreno en la Europa League, sin embargo, se saldó con un empate en casa frente a un Lillestrom (0-0) que apenas había sumado un punto en las cuatro primeras jornadas. El Rennes, por su parte, cayó a domicilio contra un NEC Nimega (1-3) que se adelantó en el 29' por medio de Linssen. Estuvo rápido para 'cazar' un rechace de Nejasmic para asentarse como 'pichichi' en solitario de esta Europa League. Menos de 10' después, Szymański puso las tablas con suspense. En primera instancia, el línea levantó la bandera por fuera de juego de Lepaul. En el tramo final, sin embargo, el conjunto neerlandés se llevó el triunfo gracias a un penalti transformado por Chery. Bischof anotó el tanto de la tranquilidad en el 89'. El AZ, que venía de caer contra la Juventus en la jornada anterior, tuvo que remontar un 2-0 en contra ante el Sparta Praga (2-4). Brunes, con un gol y una asistencia, encabezó el triunfo de los checos al descanso. Nada más arrancar la segunda parte, Koopmeiners recortó distancias con fortuna, Daal firmó las tablas con un bello remate al palo largo y, posteriormente, asistió a un Oufkir que firmó su doblete en el 84' a pase de Calvin Stengs. Bournemouth y Crystal Palace lograron remontar contra Celta y Real Sociedad, respectivamente. El Sunderland, sin embargo, no pudo pasar del empate en el Stadium of Light ante el Jagiellonia (1-1) para completar el pleno de triunfos inglés. Tras el tanto de Tuterov nada más volver del descanso, Jozwiak puso las tablas. Sufrió más de lo presupuestado el Hoffenheim para remontar en Alemania ante un Sturm Graz (3-1) que se adelantó al filo del descanso por medio de Diakité. A menos de 20' para el final, sin embargo, Hlozek puso las tablas, Conté remontó en el 80' y Moerstedt finiquitó la tarea en el tiempo de descuento. Al Torreense se le escapó un punto contra el Celtic (1-2) en los últimos minutos y acabó cosechando su tercera derrota en esta Europa League después de cinco jornadas. Dany Jean logró igualar el choque tras el tempranero gol en propia de Javi Vázquez. A poco más de cinco minutos para el final, sin embargo, Camilo Durán le dio el triunfo a los escoceses. El Ferecvaros, mientras, empató contra el Celje (0-0) y cortó un pleno de victoria que sólo mantiene el Bournemouth.

articles.title: El Crystal corta de cuajo a la Real
articles.standfirst: El conjunto txuriurdin volvió a perdonar numerosas ocasiones y vio como, tras adelantarse, un riguroso penalti de Jon Martín posibilitó el empate de un equipo local que terminó remontando
articles.summary: El conjunto txuriurdin volvió a perdonar numerosas ocasiones y vio como, tras adelantarse, un riguroso penalti de Jon Martín posibilitó el empate de un equipo local que terminó remontando
articles.body: La Real Sociedad tiene ya prácticamente imposible alcanzar el top 8 de la Europa League y tendrá que pelear mucho por estar entre los 24 mejores, después de perder ayer contra el Crystal Palace, por no aprovechar otra vez sus numerosas ocasiones y ver como un penalti con expulsión pitado a Jon Martín posibilitaba el empate de los locales, que terminaron remontando. La Real, con las habituales rotaciones de Matarazzo que dieron entrada a no habituales como Aihen, Ochieng o Zakharyan, entró bien al partido, teniendo el balón y recuperándolo rápido cuando lo perdía, como en una ocasión que terminó con un derechazo de Turrientes que obligó al portero Henderson a emplearse a fondo por primera vez. Richards, con un cabezazo desviado en un córner, estrenó el ataque de los locales, pero enseguida Oyarzabal respondió con una volea que se le fue arriba, lo mismo que le pasó a Guedes poco después. Una pérdida al borde del área de Jon Martín supuso un susto afortunadamente sin consecuencias, porque inmediatamente los txuriurdin tuvieron la opción más clara para el 0-1, un remate de Guedes desde el punto de penalti al que Herderson respondió con una gran estirada, repitiendo acción el meta local ante el luso en su siguiente intento. Un cabezazo de Mateta que desvió Sarr fue la última acción antes del descanso. La Real volvió de los vestuarios con una ocasión clarísima de Oyarzabal para adelantar a su equipo, pero estrelló la pelota en el cuerpo de Henderson, que luego despejó un potente chut de Gorrotxategi, vio como el de Zakharyan se iba arriba y el testarazo de Jon Martín desviado. Que el partido no tuviese ya un marcador favorable a los guipuzcoanos parecía increíble, aunque siendo tan cercano al de El Sardinero no tanto. Cuando Matarazzo iba a mover el banquillo, Sarr, que se había quedado en el área rival de una acción de estrategia, consiguió con un remate en boca de gol lo que los delanteros no había podido hacer y puso, por fin, el 0-1. La alegría le duró poco a la Real, porque el árbitro vio un penalti por un tímido agarrón de Jon Martín sobre Mateta, que el ariete del Crystal Palace transformó para el empate, con segunda amarilla además para el central txuriurdin. Sarr salvó el 2-1 de Kamada sobre la misma línea, pero vio como lo lograba McNeil. Pino tuvo un penalti, pero Marrero lo detuvo, aunque la derrota ya era inevitable.

articles.title: Bournemouth 'dreaming' of winning Europa League after beating Celta Vigo
articles.summary: Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after joining a select band of teams who have won their first five European games.
articles.body:
Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after staging a 10-man fightback to join a select band of teams to win their first five European games.

The Cherries trailed 1-0 to Iago Aspas' goal at Celta Vigo, and then went down to 10 men midway through the first half when Bafode Diakite was sent off.

But second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan gave the Cherries a 10th consecutive win in all competitions, extending their club record run.

Bournemouth are only the third side to win each of their first five European matches (excluding qualifiers and including the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup), after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73.

They top this season's table as the only club to win five out of five - and are closing in on a top-eight spot, which would mean they skip a play-off round and go straight into the last 16.

Some fans have told the BBC they have already booked hotels in Frankfurt for the final on 26 May.

As supporters sang about reaching that game, midfielder Alex Scott was asked for his thoughts on TNT Sports.

"Of course that's our dream. When you grow up wanting to be a footballer you dream of winning trophies," Scott said.

"Where this club has come from to where it is now, full credit to everyone who has built it.

"For players, it's a dream to be on the pitch playing for this club. We have still got wins to get to qualify into the top eight, and from there all focus is on pushing forward and hopefully we can go on and win it."

The Cherries are in unprecedented times, with their biggest trophy to date being when they won the second-tier Championship in 2014-15.

In terms of cups, they won the 1983–84 Associate Members' Cup - which later became the EFL Trophy.

Head coach Marco Rose, who replaced Andoni Iraola in the summer, said: "It's always allowed to dream.

"If you get a competition like this you want to achieve the best possible thing. We know it's far away to go. Many games. Now it's about getting into the top eight to avoid more games and then we can see step by step."

As well as just winning their games, Bournemouth are firing in the goals. They have netted at least twice in each match during this 10-game winning run.

And they are the first side to score at least twice in each of their first five matches in Europe since Queens Park Rangers in 1976.

The win on Thursday was made even more impressive by the fact they contested 75% of the game with 10 men.

It came days after Manchester United seemed to implode after an early red card against Liverpool , losing 4-0.

Former England manager Glenn Hoddle said on TNT: "They have deserved this result. They've played beautifully with 10 men - probably as good as I've seen a team play defensively and with the ball.

"I've not seen a team go down to 10 men for so long and dictate a game and deserve to win the game. They were absolutely brilliant."

Cherries boss Rose told BBC Radio Solent: "What a team, what a spirit, what an energy.

"I said to Ty [Tyler Adams] sometimes it's not about tactics and formations and stuff like this. [David] Brooks did a great job when we got one player less - he played right defender like he played it for 10 years. We changed in the right moment. Everyone did his job on a really high level.

"We were just relentless and we never stopped to believe in this win and that's why big, big, big congratulations to the team.

"You feel if you're one player down that it's a difficult night, but to handle a difficult night like this, it just shows the character of the team and of the whole group."

The coach's belief in what they are doing filters through to the players.

Amine Adli, who set up the equaliser, told the BBC: "At half-time, everyone still believed we can turn the game in our way and this is what happened.

"Everyone was like 'guys we can make it, we have to believe. If we score the game can change.'"

Earlier this month, the attacking midfielder said he saw a lot of similarities to the Bayer Leverkusen team he was part of in 2023-24.

That is not a bad comparison, considering they went unbeaten to win the domestic double, as well as reaching the Europa League final.

So who can blame the Cherries for dreaming?

articles.title: UH senior linebacker Ho‘ohuli’s journey brings him back home, close to family
articles.summary: It will be an emotional moment on Saturday when the final whistle sounds on linebacker Wynden Ho‘ohuli’s Hawaii football career. “You want him to continue to...
articles.body:
It will be an emotional moment on Saturday when the final whistle sounds on linebacker Wynden Ho'ohuli's Hawaii football career.

"You want him to continue to play on the next level, but you know how that is," Watson Ho'ohuli said of his son. "At the same time, you have to come to terms this might be the last time I'll be able to watch him play football. I'm trying to take it all in."

It is a journey that began when Watson was a Rainbow Warrior linebacker through 2004, carrying his year-old son after games at Aloha Stadium. Watson's teammates — quarterback Timmy Chang, linebackers Chad Kapanui and Chris Brown, slotback Chad Owens — would become Wynden's calabash uncles.

"When I see my old teammates, it's like we never left," Watson said. "It's that bond, that brotherhood they talk about. But it's more than that. You're playing alongside someone who's pouring blood, sweat and tears. You feel a sense of family. I wanted my son to experience that."

Watson also wanted to put Wynden in the best position as a student-athlete. There were opportunities for Wynden to attend high schools on the continent, such as Las Vegas' Bishop Gorman High School.

"I was talking to my mom and dad, and, nah, I felt it would be better if I stayed home and played in front of my family," Wynden recalled.

He attended Saint Louis School and then transferred to Mililani High School, where he was a 4-star prospect and the nation's No. 13 outside linebacker. He accepted a scholarship offer from Nebraska.

Wynden liked his teammates and coaches. But after home games attended by a red sea of 85,000 fans, he felt alone.

"I saw teammates going up to their families," Wynden said. "Me? I was one of the few local boys up there. I knew some people who had Hawaii ties, but it wasn't the same as being in Hawaii."

After the 2022 season, Wynden entered the transfer portal. Chang — "Uncle Timmy" and Watson's road roommate — offered a scholarship.

"It was great to be back, but I wanted to make sure I wasn't too comfortable," Wynden said. "I had work to do."

He moved to Makiki, sharing a place with safety Tiger Peterson.

He also overcame injuries as his role expanded. He was recruited as a "dawg" — the rush end/linebacker hybrid. Ahead of the 2025 season, he lost 30 pounds — dropping to 230 pounds on a 6-foot-3 frame — in moving to weak-side linebacker. This season he opened at middle linebacker. Now Wynden and Jamih Otis alternate at the two linebacker positions in the 4-2-5 base.

Several weeks ago, Wynden told his father he understood the wish. Wynden and Otis were football brothers.

"That's the kind of bond you get playing sports," Watson said. "It happens. In the end, you're going to miss it, like I did."

Wynden also is committed to his other team. Wynden and fiancee Joslynn are parents to two sons, Shyztynroyal and Stylenreign. They rent a house in 'Ewa Beach.

"He's doing all the things I used to tell him to do," Watson said. "When I go over to his house, I help him with the yard. He's taking out the trash, cleaning the kitchen. I told him: 'I taught you a lot.'"

Wynden said: "It's growing up. You get into that stage, and you realize, now I know why my parents did this and that. Electricity bills, rent. You have to budget. But it's good fun. It helped me grow up. I enjoy every moment of my life. My kids come to the home games. I look into the stands and I see them cheering me on. 'Let's go, Daddy.' It brings a good warmth to my heart."

Watson said he is most proud of the way Wynden navigated his journey.

"They have to experience it for themselves," Watson said. "As a father and as a coach, you can tell them as much as you want, but it's up to them to take it and find out for themselves how they'll live their life."

articles.title: Real Madrid star ‘a bit annoyed’ with his situation under José Mourinho

articles.body:
A member of the defensive ranks at La Liga giants Real Madrid is growing increasingly frustrated with his situation in Spain's capital.

The Blancos star in question? Denzel Dumfries.

Dutch international Dumfries of course took his talents to Spain's capital over the summer, from long-time club Inter Milan. The 30-year-old initially enjoyed a positive start to life in the colours of Real Madrid, establishing himself ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold as boss José Mourinho's first-choice right-back.

Recent weeks, however, have seen things take a drastic change…

With Federico Valverde having struggled to fit into the midfield puzzle at the Bernabéu, the Uruguayan has been shifted to right-back. And the 28-year-old's stellar performances have culminated in Dumfries' game time falling off a cliff.

In turn, it should perhaps not come as a major surprise to hear of the Dutchman beginning to grow restless on the Real Madrid bench. As per a report from Spanish journalist Alberto Pereiro , speaking to Onda Cero:

"Dumfries is a bit annoyed… It's not what they'd promised him (over the summer)."

articles.title: RB Leipzig's Salzburg Pipeline Has Dried Up And Borussia Dortmund Are Reaping The Rewards
articles.summary: The Red Bull talent factory once fueled Leipzig's rise, but Dortmund is now poaching elite prospects like Joane Gadou as the Bundesliga’s most famous recruit...
articles.body:
RB Leipzig once had something every Bundesliga club wanted: a direct route to some of Europe's most promising young footballers.

Dayot Upamecano, Naby Keïta, Dominik Szoboszlai and Benjamin Šeško all arrived from Red Bull Salzburg. Leipzig could identify talent early, develop it in the Bundesliga and eventually command enormous transfer fees.

Now that advantage has disappeared, and Borussia Dortmund are benefiting.

According to RB Live , since Šeško and Nicolas Seiwald joined Leipzig in 2023, not a single player has made the same move from Salzburg. Dortmund, meanwhile, has added Joane Gadou to a list that already includes Erling Haaland and Karim Adeyemi.

And Gadou is particularly frustrating because the Red Bulls knew exactly who he was.

Leipzig Identified Gadou But Dortmund Got Him

Dortmund paid €19.5 million for the French centre-back last summer. Already, the 19-year-old is showing why several European clubs wanted him.

Against Arsenal on Tuesday, Gadou carried the ball out of defence with remarkable speed before delivering the pass for Maximilian Beier's equaliser.

Beier called him an "animal", while sporting director Lars Ricken described the assist as sensational.

Standing 1.95 metres tall and capable of reaching 36.55 km/h, Gadou possesses almost everything Leipzig traditionally look for in a central defender.

He is physically imposing, exceptionally quick and comfortable advancing with the ball.

Leipzig were reportedly interested as early as March 2024, when Gadou was still at Paris Saint-Germain. His name resurfaced on their shortlist earlier this year, but Dortmund won the race.

That is what makes this transfer particularly difficult to dismiss.

Gadou was not an unknown talent Leipzig overlooked. He was precisely the kind of player their recruitment model was designed to secure.

Dortmund Have Been Shopping In Leipzig's Old Market For Years

Haaland's move from Salzburg to Dortmund in January 2020 was the first major warning.

Leipzig were interested, but Dortmund secured the Norwegian for approximately €20 million. Two-and-a-half years later, Manchester City paid €60 million to sign him.

Karim Adeyemi followed in 2022 for around €30 million before eventually joining Barcelona.

The difference is that Leipzig no longer appear to have the influence they once enjoyed over Salzburg's most promising prospects.

Twenty players transferred directly between the Red Bull clubs from 2012 to 2023. That pathway helped establish Leipzig as a Champions League regular and generated enormous profits.

Three years without another arrival represents a remarkable change.

Leipzig Must Ask Why The Pipeline Stopped Working

Die Roten Bullen have increasingly turned towards France and other European markets for emerging talent. That strategy has produced promising signings, but it also means competing with a much wider group of clubs.

Salzburg, meanwhile, has continued developing players capable of making an immediate impact in the Bundesliga.

The issue is not that Leipzig must sign every outstanding Salzburg prospect. It is that a recruitment advantage which once separated them from their competitors no longer seems to exist.

Gadou makes that change impossible to ignore.

A defender Leipzig monitored, developed under their eyes at Salzburg, and perfectly suited to their traditional profile is now strengthening Borussia Dortmund instead.

For years, Leipzig benefited from having an early view of the next generation of stars.

Now one of their biggest domestic rivals is signing them.

articles.title: Sarri: ‘Atalanta cannot always recover with comebacks’ after another wild night
articles.summary: Maurizio Sarri warns Atalanta ‘cannot always expect to resolve games with these comebacks’ after a 3-2 away to Borac in the Conference League, while Gianluca...
articles.body:
Maurizio Sarri warns Atalanta 'cannot always expect to resolve games with these comebacks' after a 3-2 away to Borac in the Conference League , while Gianluca Scamacca is 'lacking confidence.'

La Dea really are turning into the most unpredictable team in Italy, as just days after an epic comeback from 4-2 down to hold Inter 4-4 in Serie A , they went even better in the Conference League.

Borac made the most of dismal defending to go 2-0 up in the first half-hour, while Atalanta wasted numerous scoring opportunities with Jonathan Rowe and Charles De Ketelaere literally missing open goals.

It was only after Borac went down to 10 men that they broke through with Nikola Krstovic, then as Sebastijan Herrera also saw red for hacking down Nicola Zalewski, the turnaround in stoppages from Sead Kolasinac and Davide Zappacosta.

BERGAMO, ITALY – NOVEMBER 05: Head coach of Atalanta BC Maurizio Sarri looks on ahead the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Atalanta BC and FC Kairat Almaty at Stadio di Bergamo on November 05, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images)

"The truth is that we had a good performance and created many scoring opportunities, but unfortunately right now we have this defensive fragility that makes every match more complicated," Sarri told Sky Sport Italia.

"If you look at the statistics, we scored three goals on four chances late on, but before that managed to miss two goals from a metre out. We made mistakes in our finishing and continue to have a few defensive problems too, so naturally it's going to get tricky with those two elements.

"The team showed great character, as it has been doing quite a lot recently, so we have to keep working on the problems that are making our matches so complicated."

Injuries ruled out Marco Carnesecchi, Odilon Kossounou and Isak Hien, while others are making their way back from long lay-offs.

FLORENCE, ITALY – OCTOBER 29: Maurizio Sarri manager of Atalanta BC looks on during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and Atalanta BC at Stadio Artemio Franchi on October 29, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)

"We've got to keep working, try to dig out some time to do work in training, which between injuries and the fixture list is tough, but we absolutely must find a way of working on the defence and attack. It's about the movements and distribution, which certainly weren't of the right level tonight, and it has been a repeated problem in recent matches.

"We cannot always expect to resolve games with these comebacks, we've got to stop them getting this complicated in the first place."

Notably, Atalanta only managed to get on the scoresheet once Krstovic came off the bench to replace Gianluca Scamacca, while Jonathan Rowe was again misfiring.

BERGAMO, ITALY – OCTOBER 15: Gianluca Scamacca of Atalanta BC scores his team's third goal during the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Atalanta BC and Pafos FC at Stadio di Bergamo on October 15, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

"Before the season began, I'd have said Scamacca was perfectly suited to my style of football, because he is very physical and has technical quality to work with the team," noted Sarri.

"The difference is that one striker right now is feeling very confident and optimistic, while the other is in a difficult momenta and slowly trying to rebuild. I have always said that the two forwards start on the same level, and I pick whoever is in the best form. Right now, Krstovic is doing better, so he plays more, but it could just be a moment in this season that will pass."

There was tension before the game, with some Atalanta fans complaining that their buses were delayed crossing the border into Bosnia, then they were banned from visiting the city centre and corralled into the stadium by police.

"I want to thank our fans, who travelled a long way to be here and for 97 minutes gave us a big hand. Fortunately, we managed to repay them this evening," added Sarri.

This result puts Atalanta mid-table in the Conference League, after two victories, a defeat away to Ajax and draw with Kairat Almaty.

articles.title: Frank hopes comeback Crystal Palace win can be a turning point in season
articles.summary: Thomas Frank hopes Crystal Palace’s 2-1 win over Real Sociedad can help turn their season around after admitting confidence has been low.Palace secured victo...
articles.body:
Thomas Frank hopes Crystal Palace's 2-1 win over Real Sociedad can help turn their season around after admitting confidence has been low.

Palace secured victory in Europe thanks to goals from Jean-Philippe Mateta and Dwight McNeil, Frank's first since taking over as boss.

And the Palace head coach was delighted by the response from his players after going behind.

"It's a fantastic feeling to get the win in every aspect, a great feeling," he told TNT Sports.

"It's a season where the confidence maybe isn't the highest, to then go on and win the game is fantastic. We built a bit more into the second half.

"It's okay to bring energy and confidence but what moves the needle is getting the win."

Asked whether the victory could represent a turning point for Palace, Frank added: "I hope so.

"I think you can't underestimate what a win does for a group. There was more positive than negative. There is stuff we need to work on."

articles.title: Miami sends a shockwave through recruiting world, lands commitment of No. 1 overall player DJ Jacobs
articles.summary: An enormous building block for the Hurricanes was secured on turkey day.
articles.body:
Well, HAPPY THANKSGIVING, errrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrbody!!!!

While we all were stuffing our faces with turkey, Mario Cristobal went big game hunting himself. No. 1 overall player DJ Jacobs had been committed to the Ohio State Buckeyes for a long time. No longer.

He de-committed from the Buckeyes and pulled the trigger for Miami on turkey day.

The mega-recruit out of Roswell, GA was being pursued heavily by Ohio State, Georgia, Tennessee, and Miami. It appeared Georgia and Tennessee both had momentum coming towards early signing period. Tennessee especially, as he and his brother, Dawson, had visited Knoxville twice during the season, including last weekend against LSU.

But credit to Mario and his staff for getting this one done. Dawson is the No. 1 overall player in 247 Sports' rankings as well as the No. 1 player in Rivals' industry rankings. So, I don't need to explain just how important of a pickup this is. The biggest.

And now, Miami is back at the top of the team rankings for both 247 Sports and Rivals. That's pretty amazing. Not long after Mark Matthews shunned Miami for Georgia, Cristobal answers with a whopper of a pickup.

What a way to go into the weekend. Enjoy the rest of your holiday break, Canes fans. The vibes are EXCELLENT in Coral Gables right now.

articles.title: Le Bris plays down concerns after Sunderland draw at home to Jagiellonia Bialystok
articles.summary: Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris insists he is not concerned after his side were held to a 1-1 draw by Jagiellonia Bialystok.Le Bris believes the result is simp...
articles.body:
Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris insists he is not concerned after his side were held to a 1-1 draw by Jagiellonia Bialystok.

Le Bris believes the result is simply part of the process as Sunderland continue to adapt to playing in Europe and the impact of regular squad rotation.

"I think it's part of the journey, you have ups and downs," he said.

"We are building something stronger. It's really clear when you change the squad, the references between the players are different.

"I always need time to adjust different behaviours, so I'm not worried."

The Sunderland boss stressed the importance of continuing to develop despite difficult moments.

"Sometimes it's a bit harder and you have to go forward."

articles.title: Antonio Sáez, un presidente de Alcorcón… para el Alcorcón: “Quiero construir un club grande”
articles.standfirst: El empresario adquirió el paquete mayoritario del accionariado, en cuya fundación su tío abuelo, Dionisio Muñoz, fue el primer presidente
articles.summary: El empresario adquirió el paquete mayoritario del accionariado, en cuya fundación su tío abuelo, Dionisio Muñoz, fue el primer presidente
articles.body: El icónico grupo Siempre Así habla en una de sus canciones más célebres de la importancia de volver a volver. Una certeza que ha hecho suya en Alcorcón un hombre, Antonio Sáez, que ha querido “recuperar” aquello que su familia construyó y por lo que tanto peleó. El pasado 27 de mayo, Sáez se convirtió en el nuevo presidente de la Agrupación Deportiva Alcorcón, tras adquirir el paquete mayoritario del accionariado del club junto a su socio, Josu Sáez. Una operación que supuso la forma perfecta de cerrar un círculo que comenzó a dibujarse hace 55 años. Porque Antonio, empresario especializado en el sector tecnológico, no solo es “vecino de Alcorcón de toda la vida”, como él mismo se define en esta entrevista con MARCA, sino que su vínculo con el Alcor va mucho más allá. Su abuelo y su tío abuelo fueron padres fundadores del club, en 1971. Este último, de hecho, era Dionisio Muñoz, el primer presidente de la historia del Alcorcón. “Siempre he estado muy ligado al Alcorcón. Mi familia lleva cientos de años en la ciudad y tenemos un gran arraigo. Este es el club de mi vida”, cuenta Sáez. El presidente explica asimismo cómo se gestó su desembarco en la entidad para seguir con el legado de su tío. “Hace cuatro años, me llegó la oportunidad de entrar con una de mis empresas como patrocinador del club. Tratar con el Alcor desde dentro me hizo cogerle más cariño aún si cabe; y, al tiempo, escuchamos que la propiedad estaba dispuesta a compartir el paquete accionarial. Así que mi socio y yo lo hablamos, fuimos a visitar a Iván Bravo (anterior presidente) a Qatar, y en Doha fue donde surgió todo. Siempre decía en broma que algún día recuperaría el club para mi familia… y al final, pues me he convertido en el nuevo presidente”, relata a MARCA. Desde su llegada al club hace justo seis meses, la realidad es que Sáez no ha querido hacer grandes cambios. La dirección general de la entidad sigue bajo la gestión de Ignacio Álvarez, mientras que Alberto Lozano continúa al frente de la parcela deportiva. “Tenía claro que no quería entrar como un elefante en una cacharrería. Tenemos grandes profesionales que llevaban mucho tiempo trabajando muy bien en sus áreas desde antes de que entrásemos. Mi cometido es aportar más en la parcela social, con mi conocimiento de la ciudad, y también de su tejido empresarial. Creo que, entre todos, podemos conseguir una simbiosis perfecta”, remarca el presidente. En ese sentido, Sáez es ambicioso. “Quiero acercar el club a la ciudad y la afición, incrementar la masa social. Mi impresión es que podemos llegar a tener, mínimo, el doble de socios que tenemos –ahora mismo, hay en torno a 3.000–. También considero que debemos tener un estadio con mayor capacidad, y creo que un club como el Alcorcón debe tener su propia ciudad deportiva”, argumenta. En Santo Domingo, por lo pronto, el club ha construido una torre en el Fondo Norte, que se está replicando en el otro fondo. “Son espacios en los que se ve el fútbol estupendamente; y que nos sirven como palcos VIP, además de para aumentar un poco el aforo –cada torre tiene capacidad para 150 espectadores–. Además, allí celebramos eventos, lo que también contribuye a que crezcan los ingresos de la entidad”, detalla con alegría. “He venido aquí para construir un club grande. No sé si en Primera RFEF, en Segunda, o dónde. Pero creo que hay mimbres para hacerlo. Hemos hecho un esfuerzo económico importante por tener una plantilla competitiva, hemos aumentado el presupuesto con respecto a los dos últimos años y estamos muy ilusionados”, añade. A nivel deportivo, eso sí, prefiere ir paso a paso. “No quiero marcarme objetivos a ese respecto, porque no quiero frustrarme. Sé lo difícil que es la Primera RFEF. Todo lo que venga, bienvenido será, pero prefiero no pensar en ello. Además, en los partidos sufro mucho y me pongo muy nervioso. Lo paso realmente mal”, desgrana el presidente, que, sin embargo, destaca el buen trabajo del equipo en este ámbito. “El equipo es una piña, hay un gran ambiente en el vestuario. Verles entrenar es una pasada, me encanta hacerlo cada día cuando llego al estadio. Y claro, así pasa: que en los partidos compiten de maravilla, con esa garra y esas ganas de ganar que son impresionantes. Hasta les he comprado una mesa de ping-pong, que se lo prometí hace unas semanas si ganaban el partido de ese finde”, recalca. Los resultados, de momento, están llegando. El Alcorcón está bien clasificado en el Grupo 2 de Primera RFEF, donde encadena seis partidos sin perder, tres victorias seguidas, y ocupa puestos de playoffs de ascenso a Segunda división. Este sábado, visita Santo Domingo el líder, el Real Zaragoza, en un partido en el que se espera que el estadio sea una auténtica fiesta del fútbol. “Estamos recuperando la ilusión en la gente. Contra el Ibiza, conseguimos llenar el campo, algo que es realmente complicado. Este pasado domingo, con el Algeciras, superamos los 4.000 espectadores. La grada está respondiendo y es algo que nos obsesiona: que la gente se ilusione y venga al estadio, que se enganche al club”, refiere el presidente de una escuadra, la alfarera, que solo suma una derrota en lo que va de competición. A pesar de que no quiere mirar demasiado al futuro, el directivo también imagina en grande. “Mi sueño sería salir con los jugadores al balcón del Ayuntamiento de Alcorcón, porque significaría que habríamos conseguido algo muy importante. Ojalá se cumpla… pero preferimos centrarnos en el día a día y en seguir en nuestra línea”, enfatiza el presidente. Su receta para el éxito la tiene clara: humildad, compromiso y trabajo. Las mismas bases sobre las que su familia fundó el club hace 55 años. Orgullo de sobrino para el tío Dionisio.

articles.title: Bellerín denuncia la dictadura del peso entre los futbolistas: "Algunos se han desmayado por no comer"
articles.standfirst: El defensa del Betis habla sobre los paralelismo de la moda y el fútbol con el TCA (Trastorno de la Conducta Alimentaria)
articles.summary: El defensa del Betis habla sobre los paralelismo de la moda y el fútbol con el TCA (Trastorno de la Conducta Alimentaria)
articles.body: Héctor Bellerín, defensa del Real Betis en el que pensaron los Javis para protagonizar el papel de Rafael Rodríguez Rapún (Miguel Bernardeau) en su película 'La bola negra', ha hablado en el pódcast 'Fashion sucks. Renegadas de la Moda' sobre moda y las presiones que sufren los futbolistas para mantenerse en un supuesto peso ideal. El lateral de 31 años le comentó a Alba Melendo y Raquel Fernández Sobrín que "nos pesamos todos los días. Hay equipos en los que he estado, en los que te ponen multas si pesas más de lo normal. Más de lo normal, imagínatelo", y reconoce que "de alguna forma, puedes llegar a entenderlo, pero bueno, convivo con eso". "Uno de los paralelismos sobre los que más he reflexionado, que tiene que ver con el fútbol y la moda, es el tema de los TCA (Trastorno de la Conducta Alimentaria). De la gente que participa dentro. Y hay una cosa con espejo ahí gorda que...", apuntó. Bellerín, que no quiso señalar a los clubes que sancionan a sus jugadores por su peso, denuncia que "con entrenadores ha habido gente que no ha comido y se ha desmayado en los entrenamientos por no comer". El futbolista catalán ya le contó a Marc Giró, en su visita al programa 'Cara al show' que "a los futbolistas nos multan por muchas cosas, como llegar tarde al entrenamiento", "para que no nos pasemos de la raya, tenemos multas hasta por el peso, que esa es la que a mí más fuerte me parece" y que "hay equipos en los que estas multas pueden llegar a ser de cinco cifras". Héctor Bellerín comparó en 'Fashion sucks' las exigencias actuales de los futbolistas con el peso con el fútbol de hace dos décadas, recordando a las figuras de Ronaldo Nazário, Ronaldinho, Romario o Guti: "En esa época no se preocupaban para nada, el fútbol era totalmente distinto. Tú ves un partido de hace 20 años, el ritmo que hay es totalmente distinto. O sea, se corre muchísimo más, es mucho más exigente". Respecto a sus negativas a diferentes propuestas desde el mundo de la moda desveló que "He dicho que no a todas... Entre ellas tres o cuatro marcas gordas. La última igual fue una campaña de Loewe". "Soy un privilegiado que ha ganado dinero desde que tenía 16 años. No necesito nada para vivir y ya. Y la avaricia rompe el saco", reconoció.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Owners should be forced to sell, say Premier League rivals
articles.summary: Manchester City's owners must be forced to sell the club as punishment for breaking financial rules, senior figures at some Premier League clubs tell BBC Sport.
articles.body:
Manchester City 's owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules, senior figures at Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport.

This week, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) David Kogan claimed he has the "stomach" to take action against City, who deny wrongdoing and have appealed.

The IFR has the power to remove directors of a club if they are deemed unsuitable, and even force a sale in the most serious cases.

Now, executives at three top-flight rivals have told the BBC that they believe this is the appropriate punishment for City, who were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, and failing to co-operate with an investigation.

Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue

Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City

The independent commission has yet to decide on a sanction that could range from a fine, to a points deduction, the stripping of past titles, or even expulsion from the league.

But speaking on condition of anonymity, one executive claimed they are among a group of clubs who feel that City's punishment will be irrelevant unless the owners are also forced to sell. They added that anything less will make them question why they are funding the regulator through a levy.

In comments that reveal the level of anger felt by some of City's rivals, another claimed the rule breaches had undermined the league's credibility, and that they would not be able to draw a line under the scandal and move on if the owners were allowed to stay. The club were found guilty of inflating revenues and disguising losses by £900m through "sham" commercial arrangements.

Manchester City 's owners are Abu Dhabi United Group - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour.

The executive who spoke anonymously said that clubs had been asked by the Premier League to refrain from publicly revealing their views on sanctions, and let the process run its course, although some are said to have privately made their opinions clear to IFR officials. They acknowledged that some clubs were less opinionated about a punishment.

Other clubs the BBC approached declined to comment, or said they were willing for the independent commission panel and IFR to reach their own conclusions following the publication of the commission's ruling in September.

But the fact that some clubs want the unprecedented sanction of a forced sale will put pressure on Kogan to mete out the harshest penalty possible in what is being seen as a defining test of the watchdog just over a year after it was established.

It also comes amid mounting questions over whether wider UAE trade and investment in UK projects could be impacted by such a move. In September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to City's owners selling the club, adding that "they have been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester".

When approached, the IFR declined to comment. But Kogan has consistently said that the IFR will not be influenced by any political pressure.

Earlier this week he told a parliamentary committee that the watchdog would not be afraid to investigate City's hierarchy and take action, depending on the outcome of the appeal.

"Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the issue. We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," Kogan said.

"We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that's been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal.

"But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so... assuming those circumstances are triggered, if we don't act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?"

When asked how any potential legal battles with Manchester City would be paid for, IFR chief executive Richard Monks told MPs that a litigation reserve of £2m was to be built up over the next two years via the levy charged to clubs, which would be paid back if litigation was successful.

"Now clearly - and I'm not talking about a specific case - clearly, there could be a very large legal case of any particular club that would require us to spend more than £2m in terms of litigation costs and barrister costs in particular", Monks added. "So if that happens, we have agreed with government [that it] will effectively lend us the money in terms of cash flow.

"We'd expect to win that litigation, to claim costs and repay government. If we failed in that massive litigation, then ultimately it would be added to the levy and we'd repay government that way."

Last month it was revealed that the IFR would cost clubs in the top five divisions of English men's football £20.3m annually.

Last week, Premier League clubs voted to cover legal expenses for its five board directors if any of City's sponsors sued them. Two UAE-based commercial partners - Etihad and Etisalat - have both said they are considering legal action against the Premier League.

The IFR has the authority to force a sale within section 34 of the Football Governance Act which allows it to investigate whether an owner meets the required suitability standards around honest, integrity and financial soundness. If an owner fails this assessment, the regulator can direct them to take reasonable steps to relinquish ownership within a specified period before issuing an ownership removal order.

City have been approached for comment. The club previously said that the commission's ruling contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe", adding that they filed "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence [that] exists in support of all of its positions".
